**!!! MEASURE THE INK BBOX AT NATIVE RESOLUTION — A DOWNSCALED RENDER COLLAPSES IT ON FAINT ART !!!**

This cost the identification and produced a confidently wrong answer. On a drawing whose lines are
this thin, a downscaled render pushes them below the ink threshold and the 2%-of-peak bbox
**collapses to a fragment**. E-12 measured `17x38` (aspect `0.447`) at 600px wide against
`5730x2231` (aspect **`2.568`**) native — the difference between "matches nothing" and "is
obviously Driver 5-1 at `2.548`". Worse, rendering a comparison crop *from* that corrupt bbox
shows a fragment of the drawing, so the visual check agrees with the broken measurement.

**The same error inverted the Liga pair.** Native aspects give **E-10 → Liga T** (`0.783` against
the live `0.781`) and **E-11 → Liga W** (`0.859` against `0.855`); the downscaled measurement had
them the other way round. Pairing agrees within `0.006` while cross-pairing is 10x worse, so the
**aspect of the native ink bbox is a reliable product fingerprint** where the shape-grid signature
is not — a 24x24 normalised ink grid scored 91–187 on this batch (all refusal band) with nonsense
pairings, because it is far too sensitive for hairline art. Raw aspects plus looking settled it.

**Do not shape-match against drawings that have already been through the pipeline.** Flow Spine,
Flow Straight and both Prisma Links were cropped and bled by our own geometry passes, so their
visible aspect is an artifact of our processing, not a property of the product.

**!!! THERE IS NO SINGLE CORRECT STROKE PERCENTAGE — a first draft of the vendor brief prescribed
one and it was wrong for nine of the twelve. !!!**

Stroke measured as a percentage of the product's longest dimension at native resolution, against
the target taken from the live drawing each file replaces:

```
E1  0.0988% -> 0.1314%  x1.33      E7  0.1071% -> 0.2829%  x2.64
E2  0.1646% -> 0.5277%  x3.21      E8  0.0490% -> 0.1653%  x3.37
E3  0.2101% -> 0.8264%  x3.93      E9  0.1842% -> 0.4082%  x2.22
E4  0.1727% -> 0.4938%  x2.86      E10 0.0874% -> 0.4219%  x4.83
E5  0.1951% -> 0.1825%  x0.94      E11 0.0959% -> 0.4619%  x4.82
E6  0.1008% -> 0.2667%  x2.65      E12 0.0524% -> 0.1642%  x3.13
```

Targets span **`0.131%` to `0.826%`, a 6.3x spread**, because the size hierarchy places a small
cross-section large in its card and a long extrusion small — so the same rendered stroke needs a
proportionally fatter source pen on the former. A universal `0.16%` would have been right for the
extrusions and left the Venas and Ligas up to five times too thin.

**And "longest dimension" means two different things across this batch**, which is the deeper
reason one number cannot work: E-3 is a flat 2D profile where the bounding box *is* the part,
while E-8 is an isometric run whose longest dimension is however much extrusion happens to be
drawn. This is the same cross-section/extrusion split already recorded for the size policy, seen
from the stroke side.

**`E5 Flow Straight` needs NO change** (`x0.94`) — so "all twelve" is wrong in either direction,
and saying so to the vendor matters.

**Two claims in the vendor brief were verified rather than asserted:**

- **The PNGs genuinely carry no metadata.** Every file sampled runs `IHDR` straight to `IDAT` with
  no `tEXt` / `iTXt` / `zTXt` / `pHYs` chunk, so nothing identifies the authoring tool and we
  cannot re-export. **Parsing the chunk list is a ten-line check** and worth doing before telling
  a vendor their files lack something.
- **The Flow Spine fusing risk is real and correctly scoped to that one file.** E-8 is a receding
  row of about ten mounting clips, each carrying a doubled sheet-thickness line that compresses
  toward the far end; at `x3.37` those fuse into solid bars. **E-3 has the largest multiplier in
  the set (`x3.93`) and is NOT at risk** — it is a clean profile with generous spacing. So the
  multiplier alone does not predict fusing; the drawing's own minimum feature spacing does.

**Darkening is NOT the fix and was not proposed.** Half these files are already pure black at
source (darkest pixel `0`); the defect is stroke *width*, which varies `4.3x` among the twelve and
runs 2–5x thinner than the drawings they replace. An ink gain large enough to compensate would
exceed the `x1.85` ceiling at which four previous brightened drawings were rejected.

**The brief, with the measured table and the verification notes, is at
[briefs/2026-10-20-line-drawing-pen-spec.md](briefs/2026-10-20-line-drawing-pen-spec.md).**
Framer-side work (flatten, square, size to the hierarchy, ink-normalise, upload, rebind, publish)
is deliberately **not** delegated and waits for corrected files to land in `Web Ready v2`.

```
E-9  Flow 20            0.184%  target 0.408%   x2.22
E-4  Vena Mini          0.216%  target 0.494%   x2.29
E-2  Vena Round Mini    0.206%  target 0.528%   x2.57
E-11 Liga W             0.192%  target 0.462%   x2.41

```

**Every file lands in `0.098% - 0.216%`, clustered on ~`0.18%`.** That is the signature of a
single export setting applied to the batch. The targets span `0.131% - 0.826%`, so a uniform pen
is arithmetically incapable of satisfying them; the two that are right are simply the two whose
targets happened to sit near `0.16%`. **The brief's per-file table is unchanged and still the
spec** — it was right, and v2 is the demonstration of why one number cannot serve.

**!!! A HORIZONTAL RUN-LENGTH STROKE MEASURE IS WRONG ON SHALLOW DIAGONALS — IT READ E-5 AS
4x TOO THICK !!!**

The first pass measured stroke width as the median horizontal ink run and reported
**E-5 at `0.78%`**, i.e. the one file that needed no change had supposedly overshot by `4.3x`.
It had not. `Flow Straight` is a near-horizontal isometric extrusion, so a horizontal scan line
runs **along** the stroke rather than across it and returns its length, not its width. This is
the same geometry that already made ink weight "phase-sensitive for near-horizontal strokes".

**The correct metric is the MINIMUM run through each ink pixel across four directions**
(horizontal, vertical, both diagonals, with diagonal steps scaled by `sqrt(2)`), then the median
over sampled ink pixels. A stroke's true width is its narrowest crossing:

```js
const DIRS = [[1,0],[0,1],[1,1],[1,-1]]
let best = Infinity
for (const [dx,dy] of DIRS) {
  let w = 1
  for (let k=1;k<60;k++){ if(!ink(x+dx*k,y+dy*k)) break; w++ }
  for (let k=1;k<60;k++){ if(!ink(x-dx*k,y-dy*k)) break; w++ }
  const eff = (dx&&dy) ? w*Math.SQRT2 : w
  if (eff < best) best = eff
}
```

That returned `0.195%` for E-5 — and **the fact that it reproduces v1's `0.1951%` to three
decimals is what confirms the method**, since that drawing's geometry did not change. Had the
horizontal reading been believed, the vendor would have been told to halve a pen that was
already correct. **Validate a geometry metric against a case whose answer is already known
before reporting it.**

**E-9 Flow 20 is at the RESOLUTION FLOOR and cannot be fixed by pen alone.** Its ink bbox is
`1086x758` inside the 7009px frame, against `2300-5700` for everything else, so its stroke is
**2 pixels**. The next value up is 3px — a 50% jump — so there is no fine adjustment available
at any setting. It needs to be drawn larger, or supplied as vector.

### THE SET IS MOVING TO SVG (decided 2026-10-20)

The exporter asked, unprompted, whether SVG would make more sense now that he is exporting
straight from CAD rather than through the mesh-based renderer. **Yes, and the v2 result is the
argument** — a uniform pen is essentially all a CAD export can give, while this site needs a
different figure per drawing.

With vector source, **stroke width stops being a vendor round trip**: it is an attribute we set
per file, exactly, in seconds. It also dissolves two problems this file has spent weeks on —
the **frame/scale coupling** (in raster, shrinking the frame to make a product read larger also
thickens its line, which is why Flow 20 was re-sized three separate times) and the **ink-gain
ceiling** (the `x1.85` threshold at which four brightened drawings were rejected exists only
because we were amplifying pixels after the fact).

**SVG is the SOURCE format, not the delivery format.** The CMS keeps taking PNG exactly as now
— we rasterise once, at the final size, after setting stroke width and applying the size
hierarchy. Shipping SVG to the browser would be worse: hairline rendering varies between
engines, and the crop-to-frame and flatten steps are both easier on raster.

**What the export must do, in priority order:**

1. **Strokes must remain strokes** — a real `stroke-width` on the paths. If the exporter
   expands/outlines them into filled shapes, or embeds a raster inside the SVG, the entire
   benefit is lost. **This is the one thing to verify on the first file before accepting a batch.**
2. `viewBox` on the root, whole part inside it, no clipping.
3. Same views and framing as the E-series.
4. One consistent real-world scale across the set if possible; otherwise each drawing's scale
   stated. **Any single pen value is acceptable — the vendor should not tune line weight at all.**

**STEP files were offered and declined** — there is no CAD in this environment, so they cannot
be processed here. They stay as the vendor's master.

**A side benefit worth keeping:** the CAD export presents a different line set from the old
mesh-based renders (which is why the shape matcher flags these as different artwork rather than
re-exports). In vector that becomes an editable question — a designer can add or remove lines —
instead of a re-export request.

Shak reported the gap between the last product row and the black footer reading too tight on

these two pages were alone on the lower one:

| was | 120 | 96 | 96 | **`/products`, `/elements`** |
| house value | 200 | 200 | 150 | `/news`, `/privacy`, `/terms` |

Shak chose the house value **on both pages** rather than scoping it to the one he was looking at,
since they are structurally identical siblings one click apart in the nav.

**One lever: `Products Sections` padding-bottom**, six nodes (2 pages x 3 breakpoints) —
`UxP7pnItC` / `jeBJOTditUxP7pnItC` / `I3zkCZprdUxP7pnItC` and `bx7sYYpJI` /
`xWl5j5Y7Lbx7sYYpJI` / `x4KFl0Jfnbx7sYYpJI`.

**Tablet and phone each carried their OWN `96px` override, so the Desktop write did not cascade**
and all three breakpoints had to be written explicitly. The guard would have aborted had a
cascade clobbered one — it reported the original value on every node, so none did.

Verified live on all three breakpoints, with `/privacy` alongside as the control: **200 / 200 /
150 on both pages, matching `/privacy` exactly** (tablet `/elements` reads 199, a 1px rounding).
Both pages byte-stable across three fetches with no known-bad truncation signature, and **both
grew by exactly `2,950` bytes** — an identical delta for an identical one-property change on two
pages is the whole account of the diff.

**!!! THE "57px" I FIRST REPORTED FOR `/elements` WAS A MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT — the real gap was
always 120px, the same as `/products`. !!!**

An ink sweep that takes the lowest element *box* inside `Main` reported `/elements` at **57px**
against `/products` at 136px, which looked like a per-page divergence and was the basis for
calling it "the tightest on the site". It is not. `Rima 10`'s `Product Photo` is scaled to
**140%**, so its box overflows **63px below its row** while `Photo Placeholder`'s `overflow: clip`
means nothing is painted there. `2747 - 2690 = 57`; the painted edge is at `2627`, i.e. `120`.

**So an element-box measure is wrong wherever a layer is scaled past 100% inside a clipping
parent — which on this site is every product card.** The reliable reading is the last *section
box*, or the container's own `padding-bottom`, both of which gave 120 immediately. This is the
third artifact in two days from measuring the wrong quantity (after the horizontal stroke run and
the downscaled ink bbox), and the common thread is the same: **the number was right about what it
measured and wrong about what was being asked.**

### The footer Follow column is hidden — Instagram is off the site (2026-10-20, PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED)

Shak: *"remove or hide this section for now - we do not have an instagram"*.

**Hid the whole `Column`, not the Instagram link.** The column is `MgbEJ15tU` inside
`Row Bottom > Content > Right Content`, holding the `Follow` heading plus three
`Text Link` instances (Instagram visible; Twitter and LinkedIn already hidden since 2026-10-13).
Hiding only the link would have left the heading stranded above nothing. `Contact Column`
beside it was already hidden the same way, so there is precedent in this component.

Written on Desktop; **the write cascaded to Tablet and Mobile inside the same `exec`**, which the
loop surfaced as `ALREADY` on both rather than silently re-writing. Verified in a separate `exec`
and by a re-issued write (`ALREADY` x3), with the Sitemap column confirmed untouched on all three.

**The Sitemap did not move, and that was predicted before writing rather than checked after.**
`Right Content` is a row with `justify-content: flex-start` and `gap: 80px`, so removing the
second column leaves the first at `x=527` with nothing to its right. Measured after the publish:
still `x=527 w=60`.

**Verified across all 12 live surfaces:** `instagram.com/ena.supply` **0**, `Follow` **0**,
`Sitemap` still 3 (one per breakpoint), Twitter and LinkedIn still 0.

**!!! THE RECORDED "A CHANGE THE COUNTER CANNOT SEE WILL NEVER PUBLISH" RULE IS TOO STRONG —
THIS SHIPPED WITH `getUnpublishedPageChanges()` READING 0. !!!**

After the write the counter returned **0**, which by the rule written on 2026-10-19 means the
change can never reach a build. It published correctly anyway: **every one of the eight pages
measured dropped by exactly `2,840` bytes**, an identical delta that is precisely that column's
markup leaving each page.

**So the counter's blindness is specific to a page INSTANCE's `controls`, not to component
internals generally.** The `/404` failure was a `controls.variant` write on a page instance; this
is a `visible` attribute on a layer inside a `ComponentNode`, and the build picks those up —
presumably because editing a shared component invalidates every page that uses it, rather than
needing a per-page entry. That also explains why the 2026-10-13 footer sitemap rewrite shipped.

**The practical rule, corrected:**

| change | counter sees it | publishes |
|---|---|---|
| page-level layer property (padding, visible, draft) | **yes** | yes |
| **component-internal layer property** | **no** | **YES** |
| page instance `controls` (e.g. `variant`) | no | **NO — needs an editor round trip** |

**The byte count remains the decisive check either way**, and it is what settled this: a publish
that leaves pages byte-identical did not rebuild them, and an identical non-zero delta across
several pages is a complete account of a shared-component change.

This closes **A2** on the open-items list. Live `@ora.com` addresses are now the only group-A
item left — `marcus.nguyen@ora.com` on `/contact`.

### The footer logo was CLIPPED on phone — a flex-ratio column narrower than its contents (2026-10-20, PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED)

Shak: *"the sitemap section on phone cuts off the logo"* — the wordmark rendered as `ALKIM`,
losing the final `I` and the registered mark.

**It was NOT caused by hiding the Follow column minutes earlier, and saying so mattered**, because
the timing made it look that way. `Left Content` and `Right Content` are both
**`flex-basis: 0`** (`0.4fr` / `0.8fr`), so their widths are a pure **1:2 ratio of the row,
entirely independent of their contents**. Removing a column from the right cannot change the left
by a pixel. **A `flex-basis: 0` sibling is immune to content changes in the other sibling — check
the basis before attributing a width change to a content change.**

It dates from the 2026-10-13 logo resize to `127px` to match `main`, which has never fitted the
phone column:

```
                Left Content   logo   result
desktop             498         127     ok
tablet  (900)       282         127     ok
tablet  (810 min)   252         127     ok
phone   (390)       115         127     CLIPPED 12px
phone   (360)       105         127     CLIPPED 22px
```

`Left Content` carries `overflow: hidden`, so the excess is **cut rather than spilling**, which is
why it reads as a truncated wordmark rather than an overlap.

**Fix: `Left Content` width `0.4fr` -> `fit-content`, on the Mobile variant only**
(`In5qJquLmM9np7t27S`). It then takes the 127px it needs and `Right Content` takes the remainder.
Desktop and Tablet stay at `0.4fr` — writing a **non-primary variant creates a scoped override**
and does not cascade, which is exactly what is wanted here.

**The alternative was rejected on arithmetic, not taste.** Simply clearing `overflow: hidden`
would let the logo spill into the 15px column gap — which works at 390 (needs 12px) and **fails at
360 (needs 22px)**, where it would overlap the Sitemap. `fit-content` is correct at any width and
survives a future logo change.

**Verified live across six widths**, including two narrower than anything previously tested:

```
desktop 1536  LC 498 (0.4 0 0px)   tablet 900  LC 282   tablet 810  LC 252     all OK
phone    390  LC 127 (0 0 auto)    phone  360  LC 127    phone  320  LC 127    all OK
```

At 320 the logo ends at `x=157` and the Sitemap starts at `x=172`, so the gap survives at the
narrowest width tested. Confirmed by eye at 360: the wordmark reads `ALKIMI` complete with the
registered mark.

**`getUnpublishedPageChanges()` read 0 and it published anyway** — the second confirmation in one
day that the counter is blind to component-internal layer writes while the build is not. See the
corrected table in the Follow-column section above.

### THE DIVIDER STAGGER IS LIVE AND VERIFIED FROM THE PUBLISHED JS — no rAF sampler needed (2026-10-20)

Published and confirmed. **The decisive evidence is a grep of the page's own JS chunk**, which is
cheaper, exact, and does not depend on animation frames:

```
{delay:.2,duration:1.2,ease:[.65,0,.13,1],type:`tween`}
{delay:.35,…}  {delay:.5,…}  {delay:.65,…}  {delay:.8,…}
```

**Exactly five, uniform 150 ms, all `duration: 1.2` on the recorded bezier, and `delay:.95` is
absent from the chunk entirely.** The dividers live in the single chunk that contains the string
`Line Mobile Menu` — find it with `grep -l` across every `.mjs` the page references, then match
`{delay:[0-9.]*,duration:1.2,ease:\[\.65,0,\.13,1\]}`.

**A VARIANT TRANSITION IS COMPILED INTO THE PUBLISHED JS AS A PLAIN OBJECT LITERAL, SO IT IS
STATICALLY VERIFIABLE.** This file has said repeatedly that variant transitions are invisible to
the node API and that timing can only be confirmed by a human watching a foregrounded tab. The
first half is still true; **the second half is not.** Numeric literals survive minification (the
same reason the recorded bundle-scanning method works for overrides), so the delay, duration and
easing of any variant transition can be read off the served chunk. **Reach for this before any
animation measurement** — it answers "did the value ship" directly, where a sampler only infers it.

**!!! `requestAnimationFrame` RUNS AT 2 FPS IN HEADLESS PLAYWRIGHT WHILE REPORTING
`visibilityState: "visible"` AND `hasFocus: true` !!!**

Measured directly: 2 callbacks in 1000 ms. The documented tell for a frozen rAF was
`visibilityState === "hidden"`; **that predictor is wrong here, and in the more dangerous
direction** — everything says the page is live and the frames simply do not come. A first sampler
run collected **4 frames over 3,027 ms** and produced start times of `0,0,0,0,1020`, which reads
like four dividers firing simultaneously. That is pure sampling artifact.

**So: measure the rAF rate before trusting any frame-based measurement, and never infer it from
visibility or focus.** Playwright's viewport emulation remains excellent for layout; it is not a
timing instrument.

**`browser_run_code_unsafe` takes `async (page) => {…}` — a bare script fails.** A top-level
`const` or `return` raises `SyntaxError`, and an IIFE raises `__fn__ is not a function`; the body
is invoked as `await (<your code>)(page)`. **`page` is provided; `browser`, `context` and
`require` are NOT**, so a fresh browser context cannot be created from inside it — which matters
because the recorded fresh-context-per-breakpoint rule cannot be followed there. Also
**`waitUntil: 'networkidle'` times out on this site** (the hero video keeps the connection busy);
use `domcontentloaded` plus a fixed wait.

**The five dividers were independently confirmed from the opened menu**: a DOM query after a real
Playwright click returned exactly `Line Mobile Menu 1/2/4/5/6 Active`, each reaching `1506px`.
So the surviving set is right, the labels read `01-05`, and only the variant numbers still skip 3
— which remains harmless and is the documented consequence of hiding Projects.

**`getUnpublishedPageChanges()` RETURNED 1 BOTH BEFORE AND AFTER THE PUBLISH**, with an entry
whose keys are empty. It is not attributable to this change and did not block it. **That counter
has now been wrong in both directions on this project** — blind to changes that shipped, and
reporting pending work that is not identifiable. **Treat it as a hint only; the published artifact
is the authority.**

contributing nothing; the only length change is `Line Mobile Menu 3` (18 chars) becoming

divide cleanly by the expected per-occurrence change, the occurrence COUNT is the thing to
re-check, not the change.**

**Home's HTML is byte-identical at `279,198` across three fetches** — exactly as predicted, because
these names live only in the JS chunk. **A page byte-identical across a publish normally means it
was never rebuilt**, which is the recorded failure signature; here it is the correct result, and
the distinction is that the *chunk* changed. **Check the artifact the change actually lives in
before reading a byte-identical page as a failed build.**

That is this project's standing positional rule biting from a new angle: it usually appears as
"do not infer row order from sibling index", and the same applies to **zipping two independently
collected lists** — a list of "all anchors on the page" is not a list of menu rows. **Pair by a
measured geometric relationship, never by position in two arrays.**

### `/contact` nav now reverts on scroll-up, on all three breakpoints (2026-10-20, NEEDS A PUBLISH)

Shak: *"contact nav bar is not going back to original state when scrolling fully back to the top
like all other pages transition."* Correct, and it was my setting. Measured live before changing
anything:

```
at top         Nav white   rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)   transparent
scrolled 700   Fill Black
back to top    Fill Black  rgb(0, 0, 0)       <- stuck, forever
```

**!!! MY 2026-10-18 JUSTIFICATION MEASURED THE WRONG THING, AND THE LESSON IS THE VALUABLE PART.
!!!** I chose `On scroll / Direction Down / Replay No` and defended it with: *"The cost is invisible
on this page — the nav never returns to transparent, but the top of `/contact` is `Section
Contacts` on black, so a black bar there is indistinguishable from a transparent one."*

**That claim about the STATIC END STATE is true, and re-measuring confirms it**: at scroll 0 the
stuck bar is `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.99)` over a `rgb(0, 0, 0)` body, with no border on the `::after` and
the same 64px height. There is no pixel difference to find.

**What I failed to account for is that the TRANSITION is itself part of what a user perceives.**
Every other page visibly fades its bar away as you return to the top; `/contact` did nothing. A
missing animation is noticeable even when its two end states are not distinguishable — so
"the end states look identical" is **not** a sufficient argument for making an effect one-way.
**Compare behaviour against the rest of the site, not just the final frame.**

**Fixed by adopting the configuration every other page already uses**, rather than inventing a
third pattern:

| | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | `On scroll` | **`Section in view`** |
| | Direction `Down` | **Viewport `top`** |
| Replay | **`No`** | **`Yes`** |
| Section | — | **`#links`** (docY 196) |
| To | `Fill Black` / `Navigation Black` | unchanged |

`Section in view` reverts **structurally** — the condition stops being true when the anchor drops
back below the viewport top — which is why it needs no second rule. That is the same reasoning
recorded for the legal pages, and it is why `On scroll` + `Replay: Yes` was not the fix: Replay
governs whether an effect can fire *again*, not whether it undoes itself.

**THE TRADE, STATED PLAINLY: the fill now begins at 196px of scroll rather than ~40px**, walking
back the earlier "transition sooner" request. `#links` is the earliest usable anchor — everything
above it is inside the hidden `Section Hero`, and `Section Contacts` itself starts at docY 0, so
anchoring there would fire at rest. **The light photo in `Section Location` starts at 460**, so a
196px trigger still covers the one thing the fill exists to cover, with 264px to spare.

**`Viewport: middle` was considered and REJECTED as viewport-height dependent.** Anchoring on
something near docY 460 with `middle` would fire at `460 - viewportHeight/2`, i.e. ~33px on an
855-tall window — which looks like a way to keep both. But on a ~1000px-tall window that is
**negative**, so the bar would be black at rest. `Viewport: top` fires at exactly the anchor's
offset regardless of window height, which is why every page on this site uses it.

**A SECOND `On scroll` EFFECT WITH `Direction: Up` WAS ALSO REJECTED, and it is the tempting one.**
It would keep the 40px firing and revert — but it reverts on *any* upward scroll, including
mid-page over the light photo at 460-1118, putting a white logo on a pale background. The whole
reason the fill exists.

**PHONE LOST BOTH `Section` AND `To` WHEN THE TRIGGER CHANGED; DESKTOP AND TABLET LOST NEITHER.**
The documented reset is real but **not uniform**, and the difference is informative: desktop and

**!!! `/about` SHIPPED FILLED-AT-REST FOR ONE PUBLISH, AND THE CAUSE WAS `Viewport: middle` !!!**

Repointing its Section to `#about-nav-state` turned the nav solid white at scroll 0, covering the
top of its hero. The anchor and offset were identical to the pages that worked (`docY 140`,
`Offset Y 100`), so the geometry was not the problem — **the effect was set to `Viewport: middle`,
which every other page has on `top`.**

```
top     fire = anchorDocY - offsetY                    = 140 - 100       =   40
middle  fire = anchorDocY - offsetY - viewportHeight/2 = 140 - 100 - 427 = -387   <- true at rest
```

**`middle` and `bottom` are viewport-HEIGHT dependent, so a value that looks sane on one window
size goes negative on another.** That is the same hazard already recorded for choosing an anchor
near the fold, now seen on the control rather than the anchor. **`Viewport: top` is the only
height-independent setting; read it on every effect you touch, not just the Section.**

**!!! THE `Section` REFERENCE DOES NOT CASCADE TO TABLET — now confirmed on FOUR pages in one
pass. !!!** After the first publish, desktop was perfect and **tablet fired late on `/terms` (200),
`/privacy` (200), `/404` (500) and `/about` (800)**. Opening each tablet instance showed it still
on the **old** anchor (`#trigger`, `#trigger`, `#trigger`, `#section-header`). This file already
said to treat `Section` as per-breakpoint; **four for four is now the evidence, and it should be
read as "always set it explicitly on every breakpoint", never as "check whether it cascaded".**

**!!! AND THE REASON I THOUGHT `/about` TABLET WAS ALREADY CORRECT: THE RIGHT PANEL'S OWN
COMPONENT LABEL MATCHES THE LAYER-NAME REGEX AND SHIFTS THE INDEX. !!!**

Selecting "the tablet row" with `rows.filter(name).sort(byY)[1]` picked **Desktop**, because the
properties panel renders the selected layer's component path (`Navigation / Navigation Desktop`)
as a leaf element too — at `x 1287`, which sorts into the middle of the three tree rows at `x 80`.
So the read that reported tablet as `#about-nav-state` was a second read of Desktop.

**The fix is one predicate: restrict to the tree column.**

```js
.filter(e => /Navigation \/ Navigation Desktop/.test(e.textContent.trim())
          && e.getBoundingClientRect().x < 300)      // tree rows only, not the panel label
.sort((a,b) => a.getBoundingClientRect().y - b.getBoundingClientRect().y)
```

**The tell is the match count changing with selection** — 3 rows with nothing selected, 4 with
something selected. **Assert the expected count before indexing into a filtered list**; the same
class of error as pairing two sorted lists by index.

**TWO 4-OPTION SELECTS WITH IDENTICAL OPTIONS SIT IN THE SAME PANEL — discriminate by position,
not by shape.** The Overlays `On open` variant and the component's own `Variant` both offer
exactly `Navigation Transparent White / White / Black / Transparent Black`. A filter on
"4 options containing Navigation Black" matched the **wrong one** on `/news`, where `On open` was
already set. **Find the `Variant` label in the component section and take the select on its row:**

```js
const lbl = [...document.querySelectorAll('*')].find(e => !e.children.length
  && e.textContent.trim() === 'Variant'
  && e.getBoundingClientRect().x > 1280 && e.getBoundingClientRect().x < 1340);
const v = selects.find(s => Math.abs(s.getBoundingClientRect().y + 15 - (lbl.getBoundingClientRect().y + 8)) < 14);
```

**The effect popover is likewise distinguished by x, and that check prevented a real mistake:** it
opens at **`x ~1120`** while the panel sits at **`x ~1391`**, so a `Set variant...` in the panel is
the overlay's `On open` — the **open-menu close button**, which must stay `Navigation White`.
Setting it would have broken the menu on every page.

**`End` is the whole keystroke for the resting variant.** `Navigation Transparent Black` is the
**last** of four options, so focus the select and press `End` once — no counting, and `End` is
inert if the click missed and focus went to the canvas, unlike arrow keys which reorder layers.

**!!! THE SCREENSHOT-TO-CSS FACTOR CHANGED MID-SESSION AND A CLICK LANDED ON THE CANVAS. !!!** The
frame went `1459x812 -> 1512x787` while `innerWidth` stayed `1536`, so the factor moved
`0.9499 -> 0.9844`. **Derive `F = frameWidth / innerWidth` from the CURRENT screenshot on every
call** — the constant is not a property of the session.

**Inherited state found along the way, worth knowing because the three clones disagree:**
`/privacy` and `/404` already carried a phone `Scroll -> Variant` effect with its Section left at
**`Select...`** — configured and then orphaned — while `/terms`, cloned from the same page, had
none at all. **Check for an existing effect before adding one**; a second effect on the same node
would have been invisible until it fought the first.

**The verification that mattered was behavioural, not panel-reading.** The editor panel reported

**So the counter is unreliable in both directions, and the only safe procedure is the one used here:**
check pending immediately before and after the write, and treat a non-zero delta as the licence to rely on
it. That check is what made it safe to skip four editor passes. The `/404` case remains a real observation;
it is simply not a law.

### The Office/Lab second line now sits on the email baseline — one new text style, and a half-leading correction (2026-10-20, PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED LIVE)

Shak: *"increase spacing for office and lab 2nd line to match rfi and rfq email address"*.

**THE FOUR COLUMNS USE TWO DIFFERENT MECHANISMS TO STACK TWO LINES, WHICH IS WHY THEY DISAGREED:**

| | structure | what sets the pitch | pitch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Office / Lab | **one `<p>` with a `<br>`** | the preset's `line-height` | **14** |
| RFI / RFQ | **two `<p>`s in two `Details Row`s** | the `Details` stack's own gap | **24** |

So the addresses were never "spaced too tightly" by a gap value — there is no gap between them to change. The
only lever on a `<br>`-separated pair is **line-height**.

**THE PRESET IS UNTOUCHABLE: `Body Tag` (`SJt7fXVzX`) HAS 60 USES PROJECT-WIDE**, including the
`Customer Service` and `Estimating` lines in the very columns being matched. Editing it would have moved the
target as well as the thing being moved.

**AND A TEXT NODE EXPOSES NO `lineHeight`** — only `font` and `inlineTextStyle` (a live `TextStyle`). Direct
text formatting is the documented API blind spot. So the only scriptable route is a **new text style**:
**`Body Tag - Address` (`jkeGErSLz`)** — a copy of `Body Tag` at `lineHeight: 24px`, assigned to the six
address text nodes (2 columns x 3 breakpoints).

**!!! RAISING LINE-HEIGHT ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH — HALF-LEADING MOVES LINE 1 DOWN BY `(new - old) / 2`. !!!**
At `24px` the first line dropped `14 -> 19px` below the heading, i.e. **+5px**, breaking the one alignment all
four columns already shared. Compensated by taking the two address `Column`s' gap **`18px -> 13px`**, which is
the same 5px back. Both halves are required; either alone is a regression. Verified live — `gapTitleToLine1`
is **16 on all four columns at every breakpoint**, so the heading relationship is untouched and only the second
line moved.

**THE PRESET'S COLOUR IS IRRELEVANT HERE, AND THE PUBLISHED MARKUP IS WHAT PROVED IT.** `/contact` is black
with white text while `Body Tag` carries `color: rgb(0, 0, 0)` — because the white is an **inline
`--framer-text-color` override on the `<p>` itself**, not inherited from the preset. Checking that before
writing is what stopped a plausible black-on-black ship. The new style was still given `rgb(255, 255, 255)` as
defence, so it is correct whether or not the inline override survives a preset swap. It did survive, and
Framer re-emitted it **per `<span>`** around each line.

**`createTextStyle` takes `color: ColorStyle | string` and `font: Font`** — borrow the live `Font` off the
style being copied **in the same `exec`**, and pass only the base `font` (the bold/italic slots on these
styles are a mismatched family and are rejected).

**!!! A GLOBAL PRIOR-STATE GUARD CANNOT ALSO SERVE AS THE IDEMPOTENT RE-RUN CHECK — mine aborted, and the
abort WAS the confirmation. !!!** The script refused to write unless all six nodes read `SJt7fXVzX` and all six
Columns read `18px`. Re-issuing it afterwards aborted with `ABORT: zVvokwyVl style is jkeGErSLz` — which is
evidence from the live document that the write landed, but it short-circuits before reaching the per-item
`ALREADY` branches, so the other eleven nodes went unconfirmed by that run. **Put the prior-state test
per-item rather than up front if the script is to double as its own verifier**; a separate read-only pass was
needed here instead (it returned 6 x `gap=13px`/`jkeGErSLz` and 6 x `gap=18px`/`SJt7fXVzX`, the email columns
correctly untouched).

**!!! `browser_run_code_unsafe` FAILED ALL SESSION WITH `TypeError: __fn__ is not a function` ON THE
DOCUMENTED `async (page) => {...}` SHAPE. !!!** Three attempts, varying the body each time. The fallback is the
dedicated `mcp__playwright__browser_navigate` / `browser_evaluate` / `browser_resize` / `browser_take_screenshot`
tools, which work — **but their file access is confined to the workspace root**, so the recorded advice to
"pass an absolute path" is not available: `C:\...\scratchpad\x.png` is refused as *"outside allowed roots"*.
They write into **`.playwright-mcp/` in the repo** (a YAML snapshot per navigation, plus any screenshot).
**Copy what you need out, `rm -rf .playwright-mcp`, and confirm `git status` is clean** — this is the stray-file
hazard already recorded for `page.screenshot`, now unavoidable rather than merely easy to trigger.

Measured on the published page (`195,569 -> 197,110` bytes, byte-stable over three fetches, fresh
`Last-Modified`): all four columns read lines at **`[237, 261]`, pitch 24**, on desktop, tablet and phone, with

### The `/404` Return Home button removed — and the hide had to be compensated (2026-10-20, PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED LIVE)

Shak: *"remove the return home button from the 404 page."* It is a page-level
`Utilities / Primary Button` instance, one per breakpoint (`PI4P6PKft` + the `yWysTZn2M` / `frkqLd9KP`
copies), carrying `XqpXZUGU6: "Return Home"` / `NhREodF7M: "/"`. **Hidden, not deleted** — the usual
asymmetry, and it keeps the label and href recoverable. **It was the only `Return Home` button in the
project**, confirmed by a walk of every page before writing, so nothing else could be affected.

**!!! THE HIDE MOVED THE HEADING, AND THE PAGE'S OWN LAYOUT IS WHY. !!!**

```
Main > Container   h = 75vh (FIXED)   align-items: center   dir row (desktop/tablet), column (phone)
         Left Content    h 145   "404" + "You're lost."
         Right Content   h 150   gap 30   = Heading Wrapper 84 + gap 30 + button 36
```

`Container` is a **fixed `75vh`**, so unlike the project-page hides this could not change the page
height or the footer gap. But it is `align-items: center`, so **each column is independently centred**:
`(642-145)/2 = 248` and `(642-150)/2 = 246`. That near-equality is the only reason the small "404"
label currently sits level with "You're lost." — it is a coincidence of the two heights, not an
alignment setting.

Hiding the button drops `Right Content` to 84, which recentres it to `(642-84)/2 = 279` — **the
heading falls 33px while "404" stays at 248**, leaving the label floating detached above it.

**Fix: `Right Content` padding `0px` -> `0px 0px 66px 0px`** (button 36 + gap 30), restoring its
height so it centres exactly where it did. **One uniform value works on all three breakpoints**, which
was measured rather than assumed — phone stacks vertically and moves *both* columns, but the shrink is
the same 66px there, so the same compensation holds.

Verified live, every value identical to the pre-change measurement:

| | Left Content | Right Content | Heading Wrapper |
|---|---|---|---|
| desktop | 248 / 145 | **246 / 150** | **246** |
| tablet | 303 / 145 | **302 / 146** | **302** |
| phone | 230 | **259 / 144** | **259** |

**!!! THE METHOD WORTH KEEPING: SIMULATE A HIDE IN THE LIVE DOM BEFORE PUBLISHING. !!!** Walk up from
the element to the flex child of its stack parent, set `display: none`, and re-measure — a hidden Framer
layer emits no markup, so that is layout-equivalent. It gave the exact 33px shift and the exact 66px
delta **with no publish and no guesswork**, and a screenshot of the simulated state is what showed the
detached "404" at a glance. This is the same family as the recorded class-swap trick for variants, and it
should be the default move before hiding anything inside a stack.

**Measure the SHRINK, not the element.** The wrapper's own `getBoundingClientRect().height` read `0`
(the `ssr-variant` div collapses around an absolutely-positioned child), so sizing the compensation from
the button would have given nothing. The authoritative number is the parent's height before minus after.

**TWO READING TRAPS, both already in this file and both hit again:**

- **The padding ships as `padding:0 0 66px`** — Framer normalises `0px` to `0` and drops the redundant
  fourth value, so a grep for the literal written finds nothing. Match on the number.
- **`grep -c` returning 0 EXITS 1 and aborts an `&&` chain**, so the padding check never ran and the
  change looked unshipped. **Separate a count from the checks that follow it**, or use `|| true`.

**The page dropped `~30KB` (`199,208` -> `169,259`) for one hidden button, and that is correct.**
`Primary Button` now appears **0** times on `/404`, so the component's entire markup and all twelve
variants' CSS left with it. **A byte delta far larger than the element suggests is the signature of a
shared component leaving a page entirely** — worth recognising rather than treating as a red flag.

The nav logo's `href="./"` remains and is now the only route home, which is the standard affordance on
every page. Home is byte-identical at `279,553` and every other page matches its last-recorded size, so
only `/404` rebuilt — as the publish preview named.

**If the heading should instead recentre in the shorter box, delete that one padding value** — nothing
else depends on it.

### The phone footer logo was indented 22px — a dead `justify-content` my own fix brought to life (2026-10-20, PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED LIVE)

Shak: *"on the phone the alkimi logo on the footer is not aligned left"*. It sat at `x 37` while the
`© Alkimi 2026` line below it sat at `15`.

**THE ARITHMETIC NAMES THE CAUSE EXACTLY:**

```
Content        left 15  w 360   dir row   justify-content: CENTER
  Left Content left 37  w 127   (fit-content — the logo)
  Right Content left 179 w 174  (flex 0.8 0 0)
```

`127 + 15 gap + 174 = 316` inside `360`, so the row carries **44px of slack**, and
`stackDistribution: "center"` splits it **22px each side** — putting the logo at `15 + 22 = 37`.

**!!! THIS WAS A LATENT BUG THAT MY OWN 2026-10-20 CLIPPING FIX ACTIVATED. !!!** `Left Content` used
to be `0.4fr`; with its sibling at `0.8fr` the two flex-grow children consumed **all** the free space,
so the row had **zero slack and `center` was dead code**. Changing it to `fit-content` — the correct fix
for the wordmark being clipped to `ALKIM` — gave the row slack for the first time, and the dormant
centring immediately became visible.

**The general rule, and it is worth carrying: `justify-content` on a stack whose children are ALL
flex-grow is inert, and it comes alive the moment one child becomes `fit-content` or fixed.** So a
sizing change can expose a distribution setting that has been wrong since the template shipped. When a
layout shifts after a width change, read the PARENT's distribution before re-examining the child.

**Fix: `Row Bottom > Content` `stackDistribution` `center` -> `start`.** Applied to **all three
variants**, not scoped to Mobile, because it is **provably inert on the other two** — measured slack is
zero on both, so the value can only ever be dead code there:

```
desktop  498 + 15 + 995 = 1508 = contentW   slack 0
tablet   282 + 15 + 563 =  860 = contentW   slack 0
```

Setting it everywhere removes the latent trap instead of leaving a Mobile-only override. **Verified
after publishing that desktop and tablet are byte-identical in geometry** (`14/498/527/995` and
`20/282/317/563`, the exact pre-change numbers), and phone now reads `logo ink 15` / `copyright 15`.

**The simulate-before-publish technique was used again and is now two for two.** Setting
`justifyContent = 'flex-start'` on the live element and re-measuring gave `37 -> 15` and
`179 -> 157` before any write, and a screenshot of the simulated footer confirmed it read correctly.

**!!! `agent.publish({ action: "preview" })` NAMES THE COMPONENT FOR A COMPONENT-INTERNAL CHANGE. !!!**
It returned `{ type: "SmartComponent", nodeId: "CPt2kErNr", name: "Footer / Footer" }` with
`changesCount: 1`. **This refines the recorded "the counter is blind to component-internal changes":**
`getUnpublishedPageChanges()` is *page*-scoped and genuinely cannot see this, but the **preview can**,
because it reports the changed node whatever its type. **Use the preview, not the counter, to confirm a
component edit is pending** — that is a direct answer to a question this file has worked around twice.

**!!! AND THE BYTE DELTAS WERE NOT IDENTICAL ACROSS PAGES, which narrows an earlier generalisation.
!!!** This file records that a shared-component change gives "an identical delta across several pages,
a complete account of the diff". Here every page grew by a *different* amount — `/` +148, `/about` +128,
`/products` +56, `/news` +148, `/terms` +138. That earlier rule held for the **Follow-column removal**,
which deleted a whole markup block of fixed size; **a single changed CSS declaration merges into each
page's rule groups differently**, so the delta varies. The useful invariant is only that *every* page
changed, which is what proves a shared component rebuilt site-wide.

Home is byte-stable at `279,721`, the full sweep passes, and `/404` still reports `Return Home` 0.

### The dangling comma and the tablet footer margin — both closed (2026-10-20, PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED LIVE)

The two defects found while verifying the footer on desktop and tablet. One publish, one shared
component, both fixed.

| | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| **A1** the orphaned comma `c94dNo0xV` in `Details` | `visible: true`, rendering `Made in The Shire,` | **hidden** on all three variants |
| **D** Tablet footer side margin | `100px 20px 14px 20px` | **`100px 15px 14px 15px`** |

**!!! MY EARLIER DIAGNOSIS OF THE COMMA'S MISSING SIBLING WAS WRONG, AND READING THE WHOLE ROW IS
WHAT CORRECTED IT. !!!** I had recorded *"stock Ora had two links there; the second was removed"*,
with `Back to top` assumed to be that lost sibling's replacement. The real structure:

```
Details > Container > Right Content   (0.8fr, gap 10)
  Link Wrapper [CqZWv_d11]  1fr, gap 5      <- lost a child
    Footer / Footer Link - Small [uwdbJXNV4]  fit-content, gap 0
      Footer / Footer Link - Small [iHYoZv0q0]  "Made in The Shire"
      , [c94dNo0xV]                             <- orphaned separator
  Link Wrapper [m6eADuzY8]  fit-content, gap 10
    Footer / Footer Link - Small [AFK3n5kgU]  "Back to top"   <- NEVER removed, different wrapper
```

So `Back to top` is a sibling *wrapper*, pushed right, and was never the comma's partner. The comma
belongs to a second entry that once sat inside `CqZWv_d11` ("Made in X, by Y"). **The conclusion was
right and the evidence for it was not** — which only showed up because this pass dumped every node in
the row with its `controls`, instead of matching on the names the earlier read happened to surface.

**THE FOOTER'S SIDE MARGIN LIVES ON THE VARIANT ROOT, not on `Stack`.** One value per variant, and
nothing between the root and the rows carries any padding at all (`Stack`, `Row Top`, `Row Bottom`
and `Details` are all `0px`):

```
Desktop  100px 14px 14px 14px      Tablet  100px 15px 14px 15px      Mobile  60px 15px 15px 15px
```

That is why the fix is a single attribute and why it cannot cascade anywhere unwanted — writing a
**non-primary variant creates a scoped override**, so Desktop and Mobile were provably untouched
(re-measured live at `14..14` and `15..15`).

**The comma hide CASCADED from Desktop inside the same `exec`** — Tablet and Mobile both reported
`ALREADY hidden` before the loop reached them, as with the Follow column. Verified by a separate
`exec` and by **re-issuing the write, which answered `ALREADY` on all six items**; the per-item
prior-state test (rather than a global abort) is what let the same script serve as its own verifier,
the lesson from the `Body Tag - Address` guard that short-circuited.

**!!! `agent.publish(...)` IS NOT CALLABLE AS WRITTEN — IT IS `framer.agent.publish(...)`. !!!** This
file records the preview call as `agent.publish({ action: "preview" })`, copied from the docs, where
`agent` is described as a namespace *on* `framer`. Inside an `exec` a bare `agent` raises
**`ReferenceError: agent is not defined`**. There is also **no `publish` CLI subcommand** — the only
route is `exec`. Correct form:

```js
const prev = await framer.agent.publish({ action: "preview" })
await framer.agent.publish({ action: "confirm_publish", confirmationHash: prev.confirmationHash })
```

The preview again named the change precisely — `{ type: "SmartComponent", name: "Footer / Footer" }`,
`changesCount: 1` — confirming it as the right instrument for a component-internal edit the
page-scoped counter cannot see.

**EVERY PAGE DROPPED BY EXACTLY `-1,549` BYTES** (`/`, `/about`, `/products`, `/news`, `/terms`),
which is a complete account of the diff and proves the shared component rebuilt site-wide. **Note
this publish carried BOTH kinds of change** — a removed markup block *and* a changed CSS declaration
— and still gave an identical delta, where yesterday's declaration-only change gave varying ones. So
the useful invariant remains only that *every* page changes; an identical delta is a bonus when the
dominant change is a fixed-size block.

**!!! `data-framer-name="Details"` COLLIDES WITH A PAGE LAYER ON `/about`, AND THE FIRST PROBE
MEASURED THE WRONG ONE. !!!** `byName('Details')[0]` returned the **Approach card** ("01 / Research /
Color science is the foundation…"), giving a confident reading of three leaves that had nothing to do
with the footer. **The reusable recovery is to anchor on a unique text leaf and walk UP:**

```js

let foot = copy; while (foot && !/^(Desktop|Tablet|Mobile)$/.test(foot.getAttribute?.('data-framer-name')||'')) foot = foot.parentElement
const det = foot.querySelector('[data-framer-name="Details"]')
```

That names the footer *and* its resolved breakpoint variant in one step, and every later query is
scoped inside it. Same family as the `Link Wrapper` that matched the footer sitemap when the
hamburger was being probed — **on this site a layer name is a hint, never a selector.**

```
/products tablet                     rows 15..15   logo 15   stray comma leaves = 0
```

### The DESKTOP footer margin follows to 15px — all three breakpoints now match the page (2026-10-20, PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED LIVE)

Shak's call, closing the 1px discrepancy flagged when D was fixed. `100px 14px 14px 14px` ->
**`100px 15px 14px 15px`** on the Desktop variant root. The footer's side margin now equals the page
content margin on every breakpoint.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop | `100px 14px 14px 14px` | **`100px 15px 14px 15px`** |
| Tablet | `100px 15px 14px 15px` | unchanged |
| Mobile | `60px 15px 15px 15px` | unchanged |

**!!! THIS WRITE TARGETED THE PRIMARY VARIANT, SO THE REAL RISK WAS A CASCADE ONTO MOBILE, WHOSE TOP
AND BOTTOM DIFFER. !!!** A cascaded full padding string would have taken Mobile from
`60px 15px 15px 15px` to `100px 15px 14px 15px` — phone top padding `60 -> 100` and bottom
`15 -> 14`, a real regression invisible at desktop width. **It did not happen, because Mobile already
carries its own override and an override is exactly what blocks a cascade** — but that was *predicted
and then checked*, not assumed. The guard printed every variant's padding before and after and
flagged any non-target that moved; the separate-`exec` read-back is what actually proves it, since
the in-call reads are stale by construction.

**!!! EVERY PAGE GOT 24 BYTES SMALLER, AND THE REASON IS THE INTERESTING PART. !!!** `14px` and `15px`
are the same length, so the prediction was byte-identical pages with a fresh `Last-Modified` — the
documented "the change lives in a same-length declaration" case. Instead all five dropped exactly
`-24`. Reading the emitted CSS explains it:

```
.framer-7MSee.framer-12ty59o{ … padding:100px 15px 14px … }          <- base, now Desktop AND Tablet
.framer-7MSee.framer-v-p4t8j6.framer-12ty59o{ … padding:60px 15px 15px }   <- Mobile, still scoped
```

**The Tablet override rule is GONE.** Tablet previously needed its own `padding:100px 15px 14px`
against a base of `100px 14px 14px`; making the base equal to it deleted the override entirely.
So: **bringing a breakpoint into line with the base does not merely change a value, it removes a
rule — expect a page to shrink, not to stay the same size.** A byte drop after a padding change can
mean an override was eliminated rather than that content left the page.

**Verified live on all three widths** (page re-measured in a fresh context per breakpoint):

```
desktop 1536  pad 100px 15px 14px   Row Top / Row Bottom / Details all 15..15   logo 15  copyright 15
tablet   900  pad 100px 15px 14px   all three rows 15..15                        logo 15  stray commas 0
phone    390  pad  60px 15px 15px   Details 15..15                               logo 15  stray commas 0
```

and the footer's left edge now coincides with the page's own content column, read off `/about`'s
sections in the same pass (`pageContentLefts: [0, 15]` — the `0` is a full-bleed section).

**A 2-byte drift between two reads of the same build is the post-publish OPTIMIZER, not a content
change.** Home read `278,148` seconds after publishing and `278,146` on three later fetches. The page
carries `data-framer-page-optimized-at="2026-10-20T23:23:02.575Z"` — an optimization pass that lands
*after* the build, so the first read caught the pre-optimized copy. **Check that attribute before
investigating a small unexplained delta**, and confirm with the content sweep (which was identical

the replacement set is discarded. A composition scan built on it reported **`path=0 polyline=0
line=0`** on files that are nothing but polylines, which read as "the geometry is missing". **Use
`sed 's/</\n</g'`.** This idiom appears in earlier passes in this file, so any element count taken
with it should be re-derived.

### THE SIX CROSS-SECTIONS NOW CARRY ZAID'S LINE WEIGHT — and PER-STROKE INK WAS THE WRONG CONTROL (2026-10-20, PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED)

Shak: *"why do the lines look lighter than the original from zaid?"* **He was right, and the cause was my
choice of target, not the pipeline.** I solved every stroke to per-stroke ink `0.404` — this project's
recorded reference — which made the six **2.1x to 3.0x lighter than the vendor's own pen**:

```
                   ZAID pen=5          as first shipped     ratio
Vena Mini          ps 1.164 cov 6.45%   ps 0.408 cov 1.71%   x2.85
Vena Corner Mini   ps 1.099 cov 4.80%   ps 0.404 cov 1.78%   x2.72
Vena Round Mini    ps 1.189 cov 4.98%   ps 0.403 cov 1.68%   x2.95
Vena               ps 1.039 cov 4.07%   ps 0.403 cov 1.27%   x2.58
Vena Corner        ps 0.869 cov 3.59%   ps 0.408 cov 1.59%   x2.13
Prisma Multiplier  ps 1.068 cov 3.85%   ps 0.400 cov 1.36%   x2.67
```

**!!! PER-STROKE INK CANNOT SEE WHAT THE EYE READS AS LINE WEIGHT, AND THAT IS THE REAL LESSON. !!!**

Measuring all sixteen live drawings at card size showed the six sitting **mid-band** against the ten raster
ones (`0.149 - 0.674`), i.e. exactly on target — while looking visibly lighter:

```
Driver 5-1 0.149  Liga W 0.240  Liga T 0.261  Rima 10 0.355  Rima 5 0.362
SVG Vena 0.377  Prisma Link 2 0.379  SVG Vena Mini 0.389  SVG Vena Corner 0.391
SVG Vena Corner Mini 0.393  Flow 20 0.401  SVG Prisma Multiplier 0.401
SVG Vena Round Mini 0.415  Flow Spine 0.445  Prisma Link 1 0.453  Flow Straight 0.674
```

**The tell was the darkest pixel: the SVG six were `55-91` while the raster ten were `126-179`.** So the
vector drawings were **thin and nearly black** where the raster ones are **fat and grey**. Equal integrated
ink, opposite appearance. **A sharp hairline reads lighter than a soft smudge at the same ink**, because the
eye reads stroke WIDTH and per-stroke ink measures ink MASS.

**This is the exact inverse of the recorded `Liga T` / `Liga W` finding**, where thin-but-dark read as too
DARK. Both are the same underlying fact — per-stroke ink is blind to the width/density split — and the sign
of the error flips with how densely the drawing packs its lines. **For "does this read light or heavy",
measure rendered stroke width and darkest pixel; per-stroke ink answers a different question.**

**WHAT SHIPPED: a uniform `0.700` device-px stroke, which is Zaid's own mean.** Verified on the hosted
copies:

### THE CURVES WERE DASHING, NOT STEPPING — a sub-pixel stroke cannot draw a shallow diagonal (2026-10-21, PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED)

Shak: *"any way to smoothen out the curved lines?"* Yes, and the cause is not what the raster-era note
assumed.

**FIRST, THE VENDOR'S CURVES ARE INNOCENT — MEASURE THE TESSELLATION BEFORE BLAMING IT.** These SVGs are
`<polyline>` elements, i.e. every curve is a polygon approximation, so flattening tolerance is the obvious
suspect. It is not: across all six drawings the facet chords measure **~0.05 device px** and the worst
sagitta anywhere is **0.035 device px**. **That check is cheap and worth making the first move on any
"the curves look rough" report** — for each vertex triple take the turn angle `θ` and the mean chord `c`,
then `sagitta = (c/2)·tan(θ/4)`, converted to device px with `CARD / frameUnits`. Anything under ~0.2 px
exonerates the geometry.

**THE REAL CAUSE IS ARITHMETIC AND IT IS WORSE THAN STEPPING.** `Vena`'s top arc is **140 device px wide
with 5.3px of rise** — a 26:1 slope. A **0.40px** stroke can deposit at most 40% ink into one pixel row;
where the arc straddles two rows each gets ~20% and **neither row reads as a line**. So the arc does not
staircase, it **breaks into dashes** with near-white gaps. Confirmed by eye on the live asset at 8x, through
the real delivery chain.

**THE FIX: PERCEIVED WEIGHT IS `width x darkness`, SO MOVE THE INK FROM THIN-AND-BLACK TO WIDE-AND-GREY.**
A 1.00px line at grey **153** carries the same ink as a 0.40px black one (`1.00 x (255-153)/255 = 0.40`),
but it always fills a whole pixel row, so it stays continuous and the sub-pixel drift lands in the
neighbouring row as a smooth ramp. Shipped at **`stroke-width` 1.00 device px, `#999999`**:

```
                   geo (target)      centre     perStroke  stroke       cov     darkest  minAlpha
Vena Mini          17.88 (17.57)    49.9/49.9     0.510    1.00-2.00px  3.08%     156      255
Vena Corner Mini   19.25 (19.09)    49.9/49.9     0.575    1.41px       2.41%     158      255
Vena Round Mini    19.93 (19.57)    49.9/49.9     0.585    1.41px       2.38%     156      255
Vena               22.21 (21.85)    49.9/49.9     0.603    1.41px       2.53%     154      255
Vena Corner        24.53 (24.26)    50.0/50.0     0.524    1.00px       2.14%     155      255
Prisma Multiplier  25.18 (25.00)    49.9/49.9     0.593    1.41px       2.32%     157      255
```

Frames held byte-identical (`3469 / 4187 / 3802 / 4332 / 4673 / 4743`), so **stroke width and colour were
the only variables**. `geo` grew `+0.2` to `+0.35` points — the documented consequence of a wider stroke
extending the measured ink bbox by half its width each side; centres did not move.

**!!! THIS CORRECTS THE 2026-10-12 VERDICT ON SHALLOW-ARC FACETING. !!!** That note concluded *"no source
resolution fixes this — the constraint is at the display end"* and recommended either reverting the ink gain
or re-rendering with a deeper arc. **The first half is right and the conclusion was too narrow: resolution
cannot fix it, but STROKE WIDTH can, and it costs nothing.** The arc's shallowness was treated as the
problem when the real variable was how much of a pixel row the line occupies.

**THE WEIGHT SWEEP THAT CHOSE 0.40px COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THIS.** It measured per-stroke ink, coverage and
darkest pixel at four levels — **none of those three can see CONTINUITY**. A dashed line and a solid line of
the same total ink score identically on all of them. **Add a continuity check to any line-weight decision:
render the shallowest curve in the set at true card size, zoom it, and look for gaps.** This is the third
time in this thread that a tone metric and the eye have disagreed.

**A BONUS THAT WAS THE ORIGINAL COMPLAINT.** Darkest pixel goes `3-14` -> **`154-158`**, which lands inside

this reproduces the raster property deliberately rather than by accident, so the six now match the ten on

### THE RIGHT-EDGE TARGET ONLY EMERGES ABOVE THE SHADOW — sweep the threshold before trusting a bbox

A first measurement put every live photo's right edge at `99.9%`, contradicting the recorded `86.6%` and
reading exactly like the alignment having been lost. It had not: **the soft drop shadow is ink at a low
threshold.** Sweeping the background-deviation tolerance shows the real edge appear and then hold:

```
TOL    6    10    16    24    36    54    80   120
R   99.9  99.9  99.9  94.6  86.7  86.7  86.6  86.5     <- Vena
R   99.9  99.9  99.9  96.3  86.8  86.7  86.7  86.7     <- Flow 20
```

**`TOL 36-54` is the operating band**: above the shadow, below the product. At `120` Flow 20's *top* starts
clipping (`30.5 -> 46.8`), so higher is not safer. **Settle on the plateau, and watch both ends of the
bbox for where the plateau breaks.**

**The existing alignment was still intact, which is what made the targets trustworthy.** Photo bottom
against its own drawing's bottom, on the current assets: `58.7/58.7`, `62.2/62.2`, `57.7/57.6`,
`59.8/59.6`, `60.1/59.8`, `59.8/59.7`, `63.2/63.1`. So the drawings' four rebuilds since the photos were
aligned to them moved nothing material, and **the drawing bottoms are the right thing to re-derive from**
rather than copying the outgoing photos.

### CROP THE FRAME, DO NOT SCALE THE CONTENT — nine lossless repositions

Targets: left flush at `0`, right edge `86.6%` (body-right `87.5` / `88.1` for the two trailing cables),
bottom on the drawing's bottom. Reaching them by **shrinking the frame** rather than enlarging the subject
keeps the whole operation free of resampling:

```
F  = 8000 * R_new / R_target            square crop anchored at x = 0
cy = B_new/100*8000 - B_target/100*F    vertical offset so the bottom lands on target
```

Eight of nine fit inside the source frame. **`Flow 20` overflowed by 62px**, and the fix was free because
**its bottom 200 rows measure `min = max = 247,246,242`** — genuinely uniform background — so padding with
that exact colour extends flat with flat and cannot seam. **Check uniformity before padding; where it
holds, a flat pad beats edge replication.**

Verified on the hosted assets after rebinding: right edges `86.4 - 86.8` (a `0.4pt` spread against the
outgoing set's `0.9`), every bottom within `0.2pt` of its drawing, all flush left, backgrounds exactly
`247,246,242` at all four corners.

**!!! MY CORNER CHECK WAS WRONG AND BRIEFLY LOOKED LIKE A COLOUR REGRESSION. !!!** Sampling "the corners"
with `scale=4:4:flags=area` reported `249,245,240` on eight of nine masters — a plausible `+2,-1,-2` shift
matching the documented ffmpeg colour traps almost too well. **It was averaging each 418x418 quadrant,
product and shadow included.** Re-running every pipeline step on a real `200x200` background patch showed
`247,246,242` preserved identically through crop, lanczos, bicubic and `accurate_rnd`. **A four-pixel
image has no corners — sample a patch; and when a measurement incriminates a tool this file already warns
about, check the measurement before believing the warning.**

### THE GENERATED-ESCAPE TRAP FIRED AGAIN, AND THE SYNTAX CHECK IS WHAT CAUGHT IT

A generator emitting `url.replace(/.*\//, "")` into its output lost the backslash crossing the heredoc, so
all nine upload scripts carried `replace(/.*//, "")` — **a syntax error, and a malformed script takes the
relay down.** Three attempts to patch the escape failed in different ways: the anchor needs a different
number of backslashes at each layer, and an over-broad `replace(/` guard then matched the generator's
*own* legitimate regex and aborted a correct patch.

**The fix is the one already recorded and should be reached for first: emit no escape sequences at all.**
`url.split("/").pop()` needs none. The template was also rebuilt as an array of plain lines joined by a
newline rather than a template literal, so nothing in the emitted text passes through a second layer of
interpretation.

**Syntax-check every generated script before sending it**, wrapping it so top-level `await` and `return`
are legal:

```bash
{ printf 'async function __w(){\n'; cat "$f"; printf '\n}\n'; } > _chk.js && node --check _chk.js
```

That turned a relay crash into a ten-second fix, on all nine at once.

### PNG, not JPEG — and the masters are tiny

Per the 2026-10-09 correction the "upload JPEG for anything photographic" rule is retired, and a PNG
master avoids the one generation of loss a JPEG master bakes in. These renders are mostly flat background
around a smooth product and compress extremely well: **the nine `1674x1674` PNG masters are
`0.09 - 0.40 MB`**, against `0.05 - 0.07 MB` as JPEG. Both sit far below the `data:` URI ceiling, so there
was no transport reason to prefer JPEG.

Each upload script carried a **prior-asset-id guard placed before `uploadImage`**, so a re-run aborts
without creating a permanent orphan. Re-issuing two of them returned `ABORT: Vena expected PouKLVUlh0…
but has 214DWzyuIj…` — evidence from the live document that the write landed. **Put the guard before the
upload, not after it; assets cannot be deleted.**

### `E-16` RESOLVED — it drives BOTH Rimas, and the subject size is what identified it (2026-10-21, PUBLISHED)

Shak's call: bind `E-16` to `Rima 10` at full size and derive `Rima 5` from it at the established `75%`,
so both Elements rows get the new artwork and the relative scale he settled on in October is preserved.

**The subject size had already answered the identification question — the earlier reading was taken at the
wrong threshold.** At the shadow-contaminated `TOL 10` the live Rimas measure aspect `~2.0` against
`E-16`'s `0.98`, which is what made them look like different compositions. At the correct `TOL 40`:

```
LIVE Rima 5    24.2 x 24.4 of frame        ratio 5:10 = 0.751
LIVE Rima 10   32.2 x 32.4                 recorded relative scale 0.753
NEW  E-16      32.1 x 32.5                 <- essentially IDENTICAL to Rima 10
```

**So the vendor rendered it at Rima 10's scale**, and the "it is a genuinely new framing" conclusion was
an artifact of measuring the glow rather than the product. **A threshold wrong enough to move a bbox by
a factor of two will also invent and destroy identifications** — sweep it before drawing any conclusion
from a subject's shape, not just before measuring its position.

**Built by matching the live framing exactly, so nothing moves on the page.** The source was padded
`8000 -> 12000` with `#F7F6F2` first (all four edges measure uniform `247,246,242` across a 150px band,
so the pad is exact on every side), then cropped twice from that one canvas:

```

Rima 5    F = 10612  at ( 823,  950)      target width 24.2% of frame, centre 50.1 / 48.0
```

`Rima 5`'s frame is **larger than the 8000px source**, which is why the pad is load-bearing rather than
a convenience — a smaller subject in the same canvas means a bigger crop window. Verified on the hosted

### VENA ROUND MINI'S RIGHT EDGE WAS GENUINELY SHORT — correcting a verdict recorded in this file (2026-10-21, PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED)

Shak: *"fix vena round mini's right edge"*. **He was right, and this file said the opposite.**

**!!! THE RECORDED "MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT" VERDICT IS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN. !!!** An earlier pass measured
`Vena Round Mini` at `92.0%` against its siblings' `86.9%`, swept the threshold, saw `99.8 -> 92.0 -> 83.3 ->
81.8` with no plateau, and concluded: *"a soft-falloff measurement artifact, not a misplaced product — its
hard edge sits with its siblings."* **The premise was sound and the conclusion was backwards.** The absent
plateau did prove the edge is soft; it did **not** prove the product is correctly placed. The product was
`1.9 points` short, and it is visible on the card.

**THE INSTRUMENT WAS THE WHOLE PROBLEM. An ink-threshold bbox cannot measure a ROUND cap.** Every sibling
is a flat cap presenting a straight vertical silhouette — a hard step, so its bbox stabilises. A circular
cap's rightmost extent is a single tangent point where the surface turns edge-on and shades smoothly into
the backdrop, so **no threshold ever finds a stable edge**:

```
TOL                 6     10     16     24     36     54     80    110    140
Vena              88.6   88.6   87.0   85.8   85.1   84.8   84.7   84.6   84.6   <- plateau
Vena Mini         88.3   87.0   87.0   86.1   85.7   85.1   85.1   85.0   85.0   <- plateau
Flow 20           88.2   86.9   86.9   85.9   85.2   84.5   84.5   84.5   84.5   <- plateau
Vena Round Mini  100.0  100.0   86.6   84.1   82.7   81.5   80.6   79.9   79.6   <- never settles
```

**Note the `100.0` at low tolerance on a product with NO cable** — the tell that something faint reaches
the frame edge. Only `Flow Spine` and `Flow Straight` otherwise read `100.0`, and those genuinely bleed.

**THE RIGHT INSTRUMENT IS THE GRADIENT TEST ALREADY RECORDED HERE FOR SEPARATING A PRODUCT FROM ITS
SHADOW — applied horizontally.** A silhouette is a sharp transition; a glow is smooth. Rightmost column
where `>= N` pixels show a luminance step `> STEP` across `SPAN` px:

```
                  g25/4/20  g20/4/12  g15/3/8
Vena                 85.07     85.07     85.01
Vena Corner          83.81     83.81     83.99
Vena Mini            85.24     85.30     85.24
Vena Corner Mini     84.77     84.77     84.71
Flow 20              84.71     84.71     84.71
Prisma Multiplier    84.17     84.17     84.29
Vena Round Mini      74.07     82.74     82.74
```

The six contained siblings are **stable across all three settings and cluster in `83.81 - 85.30`**. That is
a real silhouette. `Vena Round Mini` read `82.74` — about `1.9` points short of the `84.63` mean.

**`74.07` at the strictest setting is not a third reading, it is the round cap defeating the pixel COUNT.**
A curved silhouette presents only a short vertical run of steeply-stepping pixels, so `N >= 20` is not met
until far left. At `N = 12` it resolves to `82.74` and holds. **On a curved edge, tune the count, not the
step.**

**THE ROOT CAUSE: the original alignment pass measured an edge definition that INCLUDES the soft contact
shadow.** That is self-consistent across flat-capped products, whose shadows are proportionally similar —
which is why the other eight are fine. A round cap's falloff is proportionally much larger, so aligning on
the shadow-inclusive edge pushed the **body** short while the measurement reported success.

**Looking at it is what settled it in two seconds.** Rendering the right-hand 28% of four cards at the true
`587` device-px card size with a line at the target: the three flat caps land on the line, the round one
stops visibly short. **Any time a metric and a user disagree, render the thing at real card size and look
before re-deriving the metric.**

**THE FIX: rebuilt from the 8000px vendor original, not from the delivered asset.**

```
source E-17 8000x8000     cap right silhouette px 4776     product bottom px 5228
was   crop 5773x5773 +0+1810  -> 1674    R 82.736%   B 59.200%
now   crop 5643x5643 +0+1887  -> 1674    R 84.648%   B 59.080%  (bottom fraction preserved)
```

`F_new = R_src / 0.84630` to land on the sibling mean; `cy = B_src - B_frac * F_new` so the bottom fraction
is unchanged and the drawing alignment is untouched. Anchored at `x = 0`, preserving the left bleed.

**THE REPRODUCTION IS THE PART WORTH COPYING: I rebuilt the CURRENT asset from source first and measured
it.** `repro.png` came back at `82.736%` — matching the live hosted asset to the digit. That proved the
whole source -> crop -> scale model before anything was changed, so the correction could be computed with
confidence rather than iterated by publish. **Reproduce the existing artifact before replacing it; if the
reproduction does not match, the model is wrong and the correction will be too.**

**It also isolated an instrument difference that would otherwise have read as a regression.** The hosted
*old* asset measured bottom `59.200` while the local reproduction of it measured `59.080` — a `0.12pt`
delivery re-encode difference. Since `repro` and `fixed` both measure `59.080`, **the bottom provably did
not move**; comparing the hosted old (`59.200`) against the hosted new (`59.08`) alone would have looked
like a `0.12pt` drift I had caused.

**Verified on the hosted asset:** `84.65%` against a built `84.648` — the delivery re-encode preserved it.
Left flush `0`, corners exactly `247,246,242`, frame `1674`. All six contained siblings re-measured
unchanged, so nothing else moved.

**THE BYTE DELTA RECONCILED TO THE CHARACTER.** The new id is one character longer at 8 srcset refs:
`/products` `289,700 -> 289,708`, **+8 predicted, +8 observed**, byte-stable over three fetches.
`/elements` and Home **byte-identical**, correctly — `Vena Round Mini` is a Fixture. Publish preview showed
exactly one `CollectionItem` change (`fixtures/vena-round-mini`), with the publish guarded to abort on any
other count or type. Draft counts clean on all eight collections; full Home sweep passes.

**!!! THE GENERATED-ESCAPE TRAP FIRED TWICE IN ONE SESSION, AND THE SECOND TIME I HAD ALREADY FIXED IT
ONCE. !!!** Building the upload script with `node -e '...'` mangled the nested quoting and produced a
syntax error; I moved the generator into a file with a **quoted heredoc**, which fixed it. Twenty minutes
later I wrote the Home regression sweep as `node -e '...'` again and hit the identical failure.

**So the rule is not "be careful with escapes" — it is: never put JavaScript inside `node -e` in this
project. Write it to a file with a quoted heredoc (`<<'EOF'`), every time, however short.** The quoted
heredoc passes the body through verbatim; `node -e` puts it through a shell layer that eats backslashes and
breaks on any inner quote. Syntax-check generated scripts before sending them — a malformed script takes
the relay down:

```bash
{ printf 'async function __w(){\n'; cat upload.js; printf '\n}\n'; } > _chk.js && node --check _chk.js
```
