latter correctly — those were done from the `Viper` folder on 2026-10-13).

### ALL 11 `/products` PHOTO END CAPS ALIGNED TO 83.33%, THE CENTRE OF THE RIGHT THIRD (2026-10-21, PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED)

Shak asked for the photos to sit better against the card's horizontal thirds. Products cannot be moved
*into* the right third without new artwork (their ink centroids span `40.8–58.7%`, geometry-driven), but
their **end caps were already within ~1.1pt of the right third's centre**, so formalising that line was
the available win. Final spread **`83.30 – 83.35`**, from **`83.57 – 85.07`** — `1.50pt → 0.05pt`.

**TWO METHODS, SPLIT BY WHETHER THE CORD REACHES THE FRAME EDGE.** The intended move is "grow the frame
to the right, pad the top so the bottom fraction holds":

```
F_new = F × cap/0.83333      d = F_new − F      padTop = bottom_frac × d
```

A pad is **lossless**, so it was used for the six products whose rightmost column is exactly background
(`rEdgeDev 0`) — those outputs are **bit-identical to the live masters** (`PSNR inf`). The other five
(`Vena Round Mini`, both Flows, both Prisma Links) have cord or glow reaching the right edge
(`rEdgeDev 16–215`); padding those with flat background would make the cord **stop short against empty
colour**, so they were re-cropped from the vendor source, where the cord continues naturally.

**!!! `body50` AND THE 2%-OF-PEAK `bottom` ARE PEAK-RELATIVE, SO THEY ARE NOT COMPARABLE BETWEEN TWO
DIFFERENTLY-CROPPED IMAGES. THIS PUT THE FIRST BUILD 7pt WRONG VERTICALLY. !!!**

Both instruments threshold against the **peak** of their own profile, so the answer depends on the
composition in frame. Deriving a crop by measuring the **source** (8000px, whole product visible) and
mapping to a **target** measured on the live asset is therefore invalid — the two readings are not the
same feature. For `Prisma Link 2` the source `body50` landed on a different module of a repeating chain
and produced a window **twice too wide**; for both Flows the mapped bottom was off by `~7pt`.

**The `grad` cap instrument is NOT peak-relative** (`lastIdx(g2, 12)` — a fixed count of rows carrying a
luminance step), which is why the caps looked fine while the vertical was badly wrong. **Check whether a
metric is absolute or peak-relative before comparing it across two framings.**

**THE FIX IS REGISTRATION, NOT THRESHOLDS — recover the live asset's actual crop window by template
search.** Downscale the source to a working plane, downscale the live asset to a template, and grid-search
`(F, cx, cy)` by SSD, coarse-to-fine. The recorded Home-card technique, applied to a 3-parameter problem.

**Constrain it, and keep a GROUND-TRUTH CONTROL in the set.** `Vena Round Mini`'s window was known exactly
(`F=5643, cx=0, cy=1887`, built by hand six hours earlier), so it measured the search's accuracy directly:
free 3-parameter search `F=5563` (**1.4% off**), constrained `cx=0` → `F=5624` (**0.34%**). Constraints came
from the record — the E-batch crops are anchored at `x=0`, and the Viper pair are 1:1 crops (`PL1` recovered
`F=1024` against a 1025px output, `PL2` exactly `900`).

**A REPEATING SUBJECT HAS MANY LOCAL MINIMA AND WILL LOCK ONTO THE WRONG PHASE.** `Prisma Link 2` fitted at
`rms 12.6` where everything else was `1.4–2.9`, and a free `F` had drifted to `872`. Pinning `F=900` and
scanning position exhaustively gave `rms 2.37`. **An rms several times the rest of the batch is the tell.**

**VALIDATE REGISTRATION BY REPRODUCTION, NOT BY rms.** Rebuilding each live asset from source at the
recovered window and diffing gave **`46 / 54 / 42 / 53 / 51 dB`** — the first attempt scored `14–21 dB`,
which is what exposed the whole problem. The interior check is stronger still: crop the new build at
`(0, t)` to the old frame size and compare to live — the six pads returned **`inf`** and the five crops
`42–58 dB`, proving every build is the live content exactly repositioned. **That makes the vertical correct
by construction**, so the residual bottom drift on `Flow Straight` (`+0.51`) and `Prisma Link 2` (`+2.36`)
is genuinely more cord entering the wider frame — **do not chase it**.

**THEN SOLVE THE CAP ON THE OUTPUT, WITH THE INSTRUMENT USED FOR THE TARGET.** One Newton step closed
`83.03–83.61` to `83.30–83.35`:

```
F_src_new = (cap_measured/100 × F_src) / 0.833333
cy_new    = (cy + bottom_measured/100 × F_src) − bottom_measured/100 × F_src_new
```

**`t` IS IN SOURCE PIXELS AND THE INTERIOR CHECK NEEDS IT IN OUTPUT PIXELS** (`t_out = t_src × F_out/F_src`).
Using the source value depressed `PL1`/`PL2` to `28–32 dB` and read exactly like JPEG loss; corrected, they
are `53` and `51`.

**THE BYTE DELTA RECONCILES TO THE CHARACTER, AND THE RESIDUAL REVEALED SOMETHING WORTH KNOWING.**
`/products` `289,708 → 289,817`, **+109**: `+52` from asset id lengths (8 srcset refs each, 6 for `PL2`),
and **`+57` from the serialised CMS payload's dedup table**. Framer pools repeated values, and previously all
eleven frames were `1674`, so `pixelWidth`/`pixelHeight` deduped to a single one-digit pool index (`:10`);
with eleven distinct frame sizes each needs its own entry and those indices grow to two and three digits.
A token-level diff summed the differences to exactly `57`. **Expect a page to grow when a change makes
previously-identical values distinct, independently of the values' own lengths.** `/elements` and Home came
back byte-identical, correctly — all eleven are Fixtures.

**A HOSTED ASSET'S BANDING IS THE DELIVERY DERIVATIVE, NOT YOUR MASTER.** `Vena Corner` measured `86.06`
hosted against `83.32` locally — a 2.7pt "regression" that did not exist. Its soft shadow is quantised by the
re-encode into discrete levels: the old asset into five (`50/33/18/9/0`, max step 15) and the new into four
(`50/33/11/0`, max step 22), and only the latter crosses the `grad` instrument's step threshold of 20. **Both
assets carry the same shadow at the same max deviation (50); the local file is a smooth gradient
(`43,42,41,40…`).** At `N ≥ 25` both read `83.32`. The rendered page shows no banding. **Sweep the instrument's
own threshold before believing a hosted-vs-local discrepancy.**

**!!! THE ESCAPE TRAP FIRED AGAIN, THIS TIME IN A VERIFICATION SCRIPT — WHICH IS WORSE THAN IN A BUILD ONE.
!!!** `c("rgb\(8, ?2, ?0\)")` lost a backslash crossing the heredoc, so JS read `\(` as `(`, the regex became
a **capture group**, and the hero-overlay check reported `0` on a page that plainly has 2. A build script that
breaks fails loudly; **a check that breaks reports a defect that is not there, or passes one that is.**
Rewritten with plain substring counts (`s.split(x).length-1`) and **no backslash anywhere in the file** —
16/16 clean. The standing rule is now: **verification scripts get escape-free string matching, never regex.**

**Delivered:** 11/11 bound and verified on a fresh session, draft counts clean on all eight collections,
publish preview guarded to exactly 11 `CollectionItem` changes all under `fixtures/`, published as
`f79b2f9cd`. Every live card measured at 391px renders its cap on the line with cords running through.
Products render `93.8–99.7%` of their former size (the Prisma Links most, at `−6.2%`), still
`1.63–2.92×` oversampled at the 587 device-px card.

**PRE-EXISTING AND NOT INTRODUCED HERE: `Flow 20` is not flush left.** It carries a **191px left margin**
(`11.4%` of frame) where the other ten bleed off the edge at `0`. Measured on the live asset *before* this
change, so it predates it; the standing "all 11 are flush left" note is wrong. It needs a re-crop of its own
and was left alone.

### THE FLOW 20 "LEFT MARGIN" DOES NOT EXIST — my own recorded finding was an instrument artifact (2026-10-21)

The end-cap alignment pass closed with: *"PRE-EXISTING AND NOT INTRODUCED HERE: `Flow 20` is not flush
left. It carries a **191px left margin** (`11.4%` of frame) where the other ten bleed off the edge at
`0`… it needs a re-crop of its own."* **That is wrong in every part and is withdrawn.** The product
bleeds off the left edge exactly like its neighbours, the crop is correct, and there is nothing to
re-crop.

**THE DISCRIMINATOR IS A PER-COLUMN CONTRAST PROFILE, NOT A BBOX.** A product that runs off the frame
holds roughly constant contrast all the way to `x = 0`; a glow or shadow ramps up from nothing. Max
deviation from background, per column, on the live cards:

```
                 col:   0    1    2    5   10   20   40   80  120  160  200
Flow 20          max:  31   31   31   31   31   31   31   31   31   31   81
Vena             max: 148  222  222  222  222  148  222  222  222  222  222
Flow Straight    max: 106  106  106  106  106  106  106  106  106  106  106
Vena Corner      max: 231  231  231  231  231  231  231  231  231  231  231
```

**Flow 20 is dead flat at 31 from column 0 to column 160.** That is product. It is simply *pale* —
`Flow 20` is a flexible silicone tape whose thin tail is near-white, so it registers **31** where the
solid extrusions register **106-231**. The alignment pass measured the left edge with a `TOL 36` ink
bbox, and `31 < 36`, so the instrument reported the tape as background for 178px and invented a margin.

**THE SAME THRESHOLD LIES ABOUT THE SOURCE, WHICH IS HOW IT SURVIVED A SECOND CHECK.** Scanning all
nine vendor renders at `TOL 36` appears to single `E-13` out, and that table is seductive:

```
E-13   Flow 20            left 730  (9.13%)     <- the apparent odd one out
E-14   Flow Spine         left   0  (0.00%)
E-15   Flow Straight      left   0  (0.00%)
E-17..E-22  Vena family / Prisma Multiplier    left 0 (0.00%)
```

But the same file read at `TOL 6/10/16` gives `left = 0` for `E-13` too. **A sweep that reports a
plateau is trustworthy; one whose answer moves from `0` to `730` as the threshold crosses 36 is
reporting the threshold, not the geometry.**

**WHAT SETTLED IT WAS LOOKING, AT 4x-8x DARKNESS.** Boosting the live card shows the tape continuous
across the card's left edge and cut by it, with the supposed "191px margin" line sitting plainly inside
the product. At true card size the tail is visible but faint.

**THE GENERAL RULE, AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME AN INK-THRESHOLD BBOX HAS LIED ABOUT A PRODUCT EDGE IN THIS
PROJECT:** a single-threshold bbox measures opaque solids and nothing else. It failed on `Vena Round
Mini`'s round cap (tangent point, no stable edge), it failed on the shadowed `/products` renders (shadow
read as product), and it fails here on a pale translucent tape (product read as background). **Before
reporting any edge as misplaced, sweep the threshold AND profile the contrast toward the edge — and
render the thing at 4x boost and look at it.** The bbox answers "where does ink exceed T", which is a
different question from "where is the product".

**Nothing was changed.** Flow 20's photo is correct as published: cap on the `83.33%` line, bottom on its
drawing, product bleeding off the left. **The ten-of-eleven "flush left" convention is actually
eleven of eleven.**

**What IS true, and is a composition observation rather than a defect:** Flow 20's left band reads
emptier than its neighbours' because its tail is pale (contrast 31) where theirs are solid (106-231).
That is the product — a white flex tape — faithfully rendered. Making it darker would misrepresent it;
cropping the tail away to start the card at the curve would enlarge the product ~13% against the other
ten and discard the detail that shows the tape is continuous and flexible. Neither was done.

### Flow 20's photo re-cropped 400px off the left — BUILT AND BOUND, DELIBERATELY NOT PUBLISHED (2026-10-21)

Shak's call after seeing the options, and it is a **composition choice, not a defect fix** — the "left
margin" was withdrawn as an instrument artifact in the section above. Cutting 400 source px off the
left lets the product read `x1.07` larger in the card while the tape still bleeds off the left edge.

**The new window is a PURE CROP, where today's asset needed padding.** Solving both conventions against
the live card's own measurements gives:

```
cx=0    crop 6956 at (0,1144)    bottom+F = 8100  > 8000   <- overflows the render, must be padded
cx=400  crop 6479 at (400,1426)  bottom+F = 7903  <= 8000  <- entirely inside the source
```

So the published asset of the morning was padded at the bottom because its window ran past the edge of
the 8000px render; `cut 400` invents nothing. One pass, single input, no compositing:
`crop=6479:6479:400:1426,scale=1697:1697:flags=lanczos`, `format=rgb24` in and `-pix_fmt rgb24` out.

**Verified on the HOSTED copy, two agreeing reads** — cap `83.500%`, bottom `59.753%`, both exactly the
live card's values under the same instruments; `leftInk` column `0`; left contrast profile flat at `31`;
all four corners `247,246,242`; `minAlpha 255`. New asset `8m1qJT9mumqkVoVeVDqy0CEBaI.png`.

**TWO NEWTON STEPS WERE NEEDED AND THEY INTERACT — do not treat cap and bottom as independent.**
`ffmpeg`'s lanczos and the browser's resampler disagree by about `0.06pt` on the cap, so the first build
landed at `83.441%`. Correcting `F` for that then moved the **bottom** to `59.635%`, because the bottom
fraction is `(botY - cy)/F` and `F` had just changed. Correcting `cy` in turn overshot to `59.811%`.
**Solve cap first, then re-solve the vertical against the new `F`, and re-measure after each.**

**THE VERTICAL IS QUANTISED AT ONE OUTPUT ROW, SO SUB-ROW TARGETING IS MEANINGLESS.** At `1697px` one
row is `0.0589pt`, and `cy = 1426` and `cy = 1427` both land on row `1014` — the target — while `1428`
drops to `1013` and `1424` rises to `1015`. **Scan the neighbourhood and take the middle of the band that
hits the target row**, rather than iterating toward a precision the instrument cannot express.

`framer.agent.publish({action:"preview"})` returned **3** changes where exactly **1** was expected:

```
WebPage        | /elements        | updated
WebPage        | /products        | updated
```

**`getUnpublishedPageChanges()` was useless here, exactly as recorded** — it returns `count=2` with both

**Two small API facts cost a relay crash between them:** `Collection` exposes **`name` and `id` as plain
properties** — `c.getName()` does not exist, and calling it throws *and* takes the session down with the
libuv assertion. **Dump `for (const k in obj)` before calling anything on an unfamiliar API object**; the
real shape is `id, name, slugFieldName, slugFieldBasedOn, readonly, managedBy`, and a `CollectionItem`
carries `id, nodeId, createdAt, updatedAt, slug, slugByLocale, draft, fieldData`. The Fixtures
`Product Photo` field is **`QsOmllQby`**.

### THE `cut 400` FLOW 20 CROP IS LIVE — published by Shak, verified 2026-10-21 (build `20:21:45 GMT`)

Three byte-stable fetches per page, no known-bad truncation signature.

```
4Yr0yro5hj5zh7U9N73uNvS6zHM.png  pre 8  ->  post 0
only in PRE:  4Yr0yro5hj…    only in POST: 8m1qJT9mum…    (22 distinct assets both sides)
```

**Diffing the ASSET SET rather than counting one id is what makes that conclusive** — it proves not

Worth preferring over a pair of greps whenever a change should touch exactly one asset.

The card renders `391x391` on the live page, first row, paired with its drawing at the same row top.

**THE END-CAP LINE SURVIVED THE RE-CROP — measured on all eleven hosted photos at the true 587 device-px

```
flow-20 (mine)     83.82        vena 83.82   vena-corner 83.82   vena-mini 83.82
flow-spine         83.99        vena-corner-mini 83.82           vena-round-mini 83.65
flow-straight      84.50        prisma-multiplier 83.82
```

**THE TWO "OUTLIERS" ARE THE DOCUMENTED APPENDAGE CASE AND MUST NOT BE "FIXED".** `grad` finds the

### THE SPEC SHEET BUTTONS — fields created, Manual/IES hidden, and FILE BYTES CANNOT BE PUSHED FROM AN EXEC (2026-10-21, PUBLISHED)

The `Spec Sheet` / `Manual` / `IES` buttons on `/products` and `/elements` were **completely dead** — 54
instances, **0** with a `Link` control set, rendering an `<a>` with no `href`. Three independent problems sat
behind them, and only two are now closed.

**All 54 are REMOTE-MODULE instances of `Utilities / Primary Button`** from **ena — Workspace**, the Ora
template author — `module:dGP0PpDpJf2SzWXgXNJo/.../dzNJ99hkN.js:default`, not
`local-module:canvasComponent/dzNJ99hkN:default`. Same trap as the `/products` + `/elements` footer in
October, on the same two structurally-older pages.

**Pre-state recorded before touching anything: [repair/download-buttons-prestate.json](repair/download-buttons-prestate.json)** — all 54 rows with
controls, variant, visibility and **instance** geometry (`width`, `height`, `position`, `opacity`); tallies

**!!! AN INSTANCE PRE-STATE CANNOT CATCH A COMPONENT-LEVEL CHANGE, AND THAT IS EXACTLY HOW THE 2026-10-21
RADIUS REGRESSION SHIPPED. !!!** These rows store what the INSTANCE sets — and every one reads
`width: fit-content, height: fit-content`, which says nothing about rendered size. **`borderRadius`, `padding`,
`gap` and the type metrics live in the COMPONENT**, so they appear in no instance pre-state and a before/after
diff of these files is structurally blind to them. The remote module was `2px` and the local one `200px`; the
diff came back clean and the pills shipped.

**So capture BOTH, and keep them separate in your head:** the instance pre-state (above) proves nothing outside
the intended set moved, and a **rendered** capture — `border-radius`, `padding`, `gap`, box and font, read off
the published page — proves the component itself did not change under you. Re-checked 2026-10-25: all **54**
instances still `fit-content / fit-content / absolute / op1`, and `Get in touch` measures **115x36** with
`padding 11px 18px` on both our site and stock Ora, so **size never changed; only the radius did.**

**Note `primary-button-prestate-2026-10-21.json` carries NO geometry at all** — only
`root, id, name, ident, origin, visible, controls`. The filename suggests a fuller record than it is.

**SHIPPED:** `Spec Sheet` **file** fields on both collections (`Fixtures gNOAfNupG`, `Elements CHPbySFRS`,
`allowedFileTypes ["pdf"]`), and **36 Manual/IES instances hidden** until they have content. Verified live —
`/products` renders `Spec Sheet` 11 / `Manual` 0 / `IES` 0, `/elements` 5 / 0 / 0, both byte-stable.

**THE COMPONENT SWAP WAS DEFERRED, AND THE REPLACE-ALL DIALOG IS WHY.** It reports **19** instances, not the
18 these pages hold: the extra are **3 in `Footer / Footer`** and **20 in `Home / Home - Projects Row 2`**,
including the three **Methodology** buttons with their tuned `IsPmXClw2` variant, `pointer-events: auto`
overrides and 60px rise. **Cancel a replace-all whose count you cannot account for** — the number is the only
warning you get. The swap is also **avoidable**: a remote instance's `Link` control *is* API-writable, proven
by the Methodology button's `/about` link, which was written through the API and is live.

**!!! FILE BYTES CANNOT BE PUSHED FROM AN `exec` BY ANY ROUTE — this NARROWS the 2026-10-11 `uploadImage`
correction rather than extending it. !!!**

That note established `uploadImage({ image: "data:image/...;base64,..." })` works and marshals payloads up to
3.76M characters. **`uploadFile` does NOT behave the same way**, measured on a 243,555-byte PDF (324,768
base64 chars — a *fifth* of a payload `uploadImage` has carried):

| shape | result |
|---|---|
| `{ file: "data:application/pdf;base64,..." }` | **`Assets upload from URL ... is not a HTTP(S) URL`** — the string is treated as a URL to FETCH, not as inline data |
| `{ file: { bytes: Uint8Array, mimeType }, name }` | **`Asset input must be a URL string, File, or { bytes: Uint8Array, mimeType: string }`** — the exact shape passed, so the typed array does not survive the relay |
| `File` | no filesystem in the exec context |

**The decode was provably correct**, which is what makes the second row a marshalling finding rather than a
bug in my own code: the array measured `len=243555` — byte-exact against the file — with `b0..b3 = 37,80,68,70`,
i.e. `%PDF`.

**`atob` DOES NOT EXIST in the exec context.** A first attempt returned `ABORT: no atob`; the base64 had to be
decoded with a hand-written table. Worth knowing before assuming any browser global is available there.

**So a PDF reaches Framer only two ways: a PUBLIC HTTPS URL that Framer fetches server-side, or a hand drop in
the editor.** Localhost will not do — the fetch is server-side, as already recorded for `uploadImage`. This is
the same wall as video, and the practical consequence is identical: **the asset step needs Shak, the rest is
scriptable.**

**A `file` field is still the right shape despite that**, and the reasoning is worth keeping: if the PDF has to
be dropped in by hand regardless, dropping it into the CMS cell is strictly better than hosting it elsewhere
and pasting a URL into a `link` field. The failed upload route does not argue for changing the field type.

**STILL OPEN, AND IT IS ONE EDITOR CHECK: can a button's `Link` control bind to a `file` field?** The recorded
binding rule is strict type matching — a `string` control takes `string` fields, an `Image` control takes
`image` fields, and a Video's `Source: Upload` **File** control binds **nothing at all**. By that pattern a
`file` field may not be offered to a Link control either. **The binding menu answers it instantly and the ARROW
is the tell** — arrow-less means bindable, an arrow means predicates only. If it is not offered, the fallback
is a `link` field holding the PDF URL, which is certainly bindable.

**A per-product link MUST be a CMS binding, so the API cannot finish this.** `setAttributes` can only write a
literal — the same URL on every instance. That is the whole reason this ends in the editor.

**!!! A NEW EDITOR FAILURE SIGNATURE: the renderer can report HEALTHY while being unusable. !!!** Mid-session
the editor went to **`innerWidth: 0, innerHeight: 0`** with `document.visibilityState: "visible"`,
`hasFocus(): true`, `readyState: "complete"` and **3,278 divs** — so every liveness check passes.
`Page.captureScreenshot` timed out repeatedly, and `getBoundingClientRect` returned garbage (page layers at
`x: -222, y: 30024`). **A zero-sized viewport makes every coordinate meaningless while the DOM still reads as
live**, so the recorded "assert the document contains the tree" check does NOT catch it. **Read `innerWidth`
before driving the panel, and stop when it is 0** — with no screenshot to verify against, a click lands
somewhere unknown, and this is the condition under which stray keystrokes delete layers.

**`Alkimi_SpecSheet_Master.pdf` IS A BLANK TEMPLATE, not a product sheet.** 5 pages, custom `654 x 834pt`,
Gellix throughout (so it is genuine Alkimi artwork), no images, 243 KB. Its text is `PRODUCT NAME`,
`PRODUCT DESCRIPTOR`, `Insert Text` x60, `0.0 W/ft`, `00 lm/ft`, `0000k`, lorem ipsum, and the InDesign slug
`Alkimi_SpecSheet_Master.indd` printed on each page. Structure: cover -> product specifications -> compatible
extrusions -> driver -> driver specifications, with *"Find compatible extrusions on the following page"*.

**That structure says the deliverable is a COMBINATION sheet, not a per-SKU one** — a light source paired with
extrusions and a driver. It matches the filenames already in `Downloads`:
`Alkimi — Rimi COB + Prisma Multiplier Spec Sheet.pdf` and `Alkimi — Rimi COB + Vena 1 Profile Spec Sheet.pdf`.
A per-product library also exists under `Marketing/Alkimi_Munayki/Spec Sheets/`. **So the CMS field will not
map one-to-one onto products, and that should be settled before 16 PDFs are collected.**

**Extracting PDF text: scan for string literals manually, do not regex.** A `(...)` literal can nest and can
contain escaped parens, and every regex attempt here lost a backslash crossing the heredoc. A character scan
tracking depth, with `String.fromCharCode(92)` for the backslash, has no escapes in it at all and worked first
time. Content streams are `FlateDecode`, so inflate each `stream`/`endstream` span and keep the ones
containing `Tj`/`TJ`.

**The generated-escape trap fired TWICE more in one session**, both caught by the syntax check before reaching
the relay. The standing rule held: **emit no escape sequences at all** — a `"   /   "` separator needs none
where a newline cannot survive. **`sed` is not the fix** — patching the generator with `sed` produced a worse
break than the original. Rewrite the generator from a quoted heredoc instead.

### !!! FRAMER EMITS `target="_blank"` ITSELF FOR A FILE-ASSET LINK — my prediction was WRONG (2026-10-21) !!!

The first real Spec Sheet PDF went into `Fixtures / prisma-multiplier` and the published page answers the
original question outright:

```html
<a data-framer-name="Button Blue to White"
   href="https://framerusercontent.com/assets/rlsA4b7Tmu1FU5c40SX2xuPBM8M.pdf"
   target="_blank" tabindex="0" style="…background-color:rgb(53, 121, 11)…">
```

**`target="_blank"` appears exactly once on the page — on this link — and nothing of ours put it there.**
So a `Link` control that resolves to a **file** asset opens in a new tab automatically, and the "open a new
browser tab with our spec sheet" request is satisfied with no further work: no local-component swap, no code
override, no `19`-instance replace-all.

**WHY I GOT IT WRONG, AND IT IS A REASONING ERROR WORTH NAMING.** I measured the asset headers —

```
Content-Type: application/pdf    Content-Length: 243555
Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable    X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
```

— found **no `Content-Disposition`**, and concluded the PDF would open in the **current** tab. The header
evidence was correct and the conclusion did not follow. **`Content-Disposition` governs RENDER vs DOWNLOAD;
`target` governs WHICH TAB.** They are independent axes and I collapsed them into one. Having established a
real fact about the server I stopped looking at what the *client* markup does — when the decisive evidence
(the emitted `<a>`) was one publish away and I had already told Shak it was only observable after a publish.
**When a question has two independent mechanisms, measuring one of them is not a partial answer — it is no
answer.**

**The server finding still stands and is still useful:** with no `Content-Disposition` the PDF *renders* in
the browser's viewer rather than downloading. Combined with the automatic `target`, the visitor gets the
spec sheet in a new tab and keeps the product page — the best of the outcomes that were on the table.

**`rel="noopener"` is absent** (`noopener` count 0). Not a live risk: Chrome 88+, Firefox 79+ and Safari
12.1+ all imply `noopener` for `target="_blank"`. Recorded only so a future audit does not re-flag it.

**A `file` CMS field READS BACK AS AN OBJECT, not a string** — `{ id, url, extension }`, e.g.
`{"id":"rlsA4b7Tmu….pdf","url":"https://framerusercontent.com/assets/rlsA4b7Tmu….pdf","extension":"pdf"}`.
That matches the 2026-10-12 correction for **image** fields and extends it to file fields: **object out,
URL string in.** Read `value.url`, and accept either (`typeof v === "string" ? v : v.url`).

**The other ten buttons are unaffected and render cleanly.** `>Spec Sheet<` 11, asset refs 2 (the anchor plus
the serialised CMS payload), `target="_blank"` 1 — so Framer omits the href entirely for the ten items with
no file, exactly as recorded for an unresolvable CMS link. `/products` `266,928 -> 267,124` (+196).

**The uploaded file is the blank master** — `Content-Length: 243555`, byte-exact against
`Alkimi_SpecSheet_Master.pdf`. Correct as a mechanism test; it is the 5-page `PRODUCT NAME` / `Insert Text`
template, not a finished sheet.

**Home was re-checked in the same pass** because Framer's own agent had an un-reverted hero change pending:
`278,093 -> 278,073` (-20), with Gellix **58**, `H1 Hero` **2**, `H1 Hero - Style` **2**, the old shared
`sA1pdkMlu` **0**, `--framer-font-size:72px` **2**, `Measured` **2**, `lighting objects.` **2**. The hero is
intact on its own presets; nothing regressed.

### The Spec Sheet buttons go GREEN → BLACK on hover — scoped to them alone (2026-10-21, PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED LIVE)

Shak's screenshot of a white "Spec Sheet" pill was the button's **hover** state, not its rest state — measured before
anything was changed. Rest was already green; the ask was to replace the white hover with black, **without** touching
the footer `Get in touch`, which shares the same variant and must keep green→white.

**THE COMPONENT EXISTS IN THREE SEPARATE MODULES, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES SCOPING POSSIBLE AT ALL.** A full
93-instance walk (`controls.variant` against the 12 known variant ids, plus `componentIdentifier` containing
`dzNJ99hkN`):

| module | instances | contents |
|---|---|---|
| `module:dGP0PpDpJf2SzWXgXNJo/…/dzNJ99hkN.js` | **57** | 18 Spec Sheet + 18 Manual + 18 IES + 3 `Get in touch` |
| `local-module:canvasComponent/dzNJ99hkN` | 16 | `/404`, `/careers`, Section CTA, grid cards |
| `module:iwulOY7vxTPBNW5DchJh/…/dzNJ99hkN.js` | 20 | Home Row 2 — **Methodology x3** + `View Case Study` x17 |

**CORRECTION: this file recorded the Methodology buttons as local. They are not — they are on a THIRD remote module.**
That matters because it means a replace-all on the download buttons cannot reach them, which is what made the whole
job safe. Pre-state at [repair/primary-button-prestate-2026-10-21.json](repair/primary-button-prestate-2026-10-21.json).

**!!! THE 2026-10-07 "`variant` CONTROL CANNOT BE WRITTEN" EPISODE IS NOW FULLY EXPLAINED, AND BOTH HALVES WERE
MISDIAGNOSED. !!!** That note recorded two walls — the control is unwritable, and an `addVariant` variant is never
offered to instances. The real rule, demonstrated here:

- **`variant` IS writable**, to any variant that exists in the target instance's **own compiled module**.
- An **`addVariant`-created** variant is never compiled in, so it is offered to nothing — that is the single cause.
- A variant created by **editor `Ctrl+D`** IS compiled in, and instances take it first time.

So the one-token `Ora Blue` repoint that turned **9 buttons green site-wide** when the ask was scoped to one was
unnecessary. **Re-test a "not possible" verdict built on one failed attempt before designing around it.**

**THE PLAN, AND WHY EACH STEP WAS FORCED.** The 12 stock variants hold no green→black pair, and a new variant can only
live in the local component — so the 57 remote instances had to be swapped to local first, then pointed at it.

1. `Ctrl+D` on `Button White to Black` → rename `Button Blue to Black` (`KaTzNfkSG`), fill = the live `Alkimi Green`
   ColorStyle **borrowed off `PQb6JRcY1` in the same `exec`** (a literal fails silently), label → white.
2. Replace all instances → `Project / Utilities / Primary Button`.
3. Write the 18 Spec Sheet instances to `KaTzNfkSG`.
4. Give the new variant its own hover partner (see below).

**THE REPLACE-ALL DIALOG SAID "19 INSTANCES" AND 19 RECONCILES EXACTLY.** Framer counts **logical** instances and
treats breakpoint copies as derived: `/products` 3 Collection Lists x 3 button types = 9, `/elements` the same = 9,
plus 1 footer `Get in touch` = **19 logical = 57 instances**. The standing rule is to cancel a replace-all whose count
you cannot account for; **account for it by dividing by 3 and counting Collection List templates**, not by assuming.

**!!! THE SWAP GIVES EVERY INSTANCE A NEW ID — a per-id restore from the pre-state is impossible. !!!** All 57 recorded
ids came back `MISSING`, which reads exactly like catastrophic loss. Nothing was lost: the nodes were replaced.
**Diff by (root, title, variant, visible, origin) instead of by id** — that showed the only change across all 93
instances was `REMOTE → LOCAL` on exactly the 57, with **36 instances in byte-identical groups**.

**AND THIS TIME THE SWAP PRESERVED EVERYTHING — contradicting the 2026-10-13 footer swap, which reset `variant` on
all 6.** Titles, variants, visibility and — the real risk — **the six CMS Link bindings** all survived, confirmed by
the blue `Spec Sheet` pill on two separate Collection List templates and by the published field-id count
(`gNOAfNupG` still **14** on `/products`, `CHPbySFRS` **8** on `/elements`). **So a replace-all's collateral damage is
not predictable from precedent; capture the pre-state and diff, every time.**

**!!! A HOVER VARIANT IS HARD-WIRED TO ONE REST PARTNER BY AN EXPLICIT `Leave` INTERACTION — borrowing another pair's
hover variant leaves the button on the WRONG rest state. !!!**

The first publish looked right and was wrong in a way no static check could see:

```
REST     Button Blue to Black          rgb(53, 121, 11)   green    correct
HOVER    Button White to Black - Hover rgb(0, 0, 0)       black    correct
UNHOVER  Button White to Black         rgb(255, 255, 255) WHITE    <- defect
```

Reading the hover variants' panels explains it: **every one carries `Leave → <its own rest variant>`**
(`Button White to Black - Hover` → `Button White to Black`; `Button Blue to White - Hover` → `Button Blue to White`).
The return is **not** automatic. So a new rest variant needs its **own** duplicated hover partner, with `Leave`
repointed at it and the rest variant's `Enter` repointed at the partner. Built `Button Blue to Black - Hover`
(`xDpnhBaOq`): black fill and white label inherited, two dropdown edits.

**The interaction target IS a native `<select>` listing every variant by id**, so the native-setter route works — but
`select.value` reads back stale immediately after, so **close the popover and reopen it to verify** (the panel then
read `Leave → Button Blue to Black` and `Enter → Button Blue to Black - Hover`).

**!!! I DUPLICATED THE WRONG VARIANT BY REUSING A LAYER-TREE COORDINATE ACROSS A SELECTION. !!!** Selecting a row
auto-expands it and shifts everything below; my second click landed on `Button White to Black` instead of its hover
partner, and the duplicate came out **white** (`bg=rgb(255,255,255)`) rather than black. This file already warns
"re-derive row positions after every selection" — **the concrete discipline is: read rows, click, verify the selection
by a property only the intended row has, and only then press the key.** Verifying by the zoomed row label is NOT
enough: the panel truncates to `Button White t...`, which matches four variants. The `Leave → Button White to Black`
reading is what identified it unambiguously.

**A COMPONENT VARIANT CAN BE DELETED FROM THE EDITOR WITH THE `Delete` KEY**, even though `removeNodes` and
`node.remove()` both fail on component internals through the API. The stray was renamed `DELETE ME - wrong copy`
first (names are API-writable) so the tree row was unmistakable, then selected, confirmed by the purple highlight, and
deleted — 13 variants again. **So an API-created stray does not have to wait for Shak; mark it, verify, delete.**

**`inlineTextStyle` ON A VARIANT'S TEXT NODE FAILS SILENTLY.** The write reported success and the canvas was unchanged
after a 10s wait at two zoom levels. The editor route works: select the text layer **from the Layers panel** (a
canvas double-click plus a panel scroll opened the component's variables dialog instead), then the `Color` row — whose
hex field **does not exist as an `<input>` until clicked**, at which point a colour popover opens with the hex and an
alpha field. `ctrl+a` is safe there only because `document.activeElement` was asserted to be that input first.

**!!! THE PUBLISH PREVIEW IS SUBJECT TO SESSION STALENESS, AND A STALE SESSION REPORTS `changesCount=0`. !!!** After
the interaction edits an older session returned **0** — indistinguishable from "this change will never publish", the

**VERIFIED LIVE WITH A REAL POINTER, which is the only way to observe a Framer variant interaction:**

| **Spec Sheet** (18) | green `rgb(53,121,11)`, white label | **black `rgb(0,0,0)`**, white label | **green** |

**!!! THE SWAP TURNED ALL 57 BUTTONS FROM A 2px ROUNDED RECTANGLE INTO A 200px PILL, AND I SHIPPED IT. Fixed
2026-10-21, published `025cab3c9`. !!!**

Shak spotted it ("the buttons had a rectangle appearance with rounded corners"). The two modules are **NOT**
geometrically identical:

| | `border-radius` |
|---|---|
| remote `dGP0PpDpJf2SzWXgXNJo` (where the 57 lived) | **`2px`** |
| `local-module:canvasComponent/dzNJ99hkN` | **`200px`** |

**The error was checking the wrong pair.** On 2026-10-20 I verified that the four *local* candidate variants were

"the switch changes fill and border and nothing else". That was a comparison **within** the local component; I never

variant-scoped radius on the Home cards.

### The phone Spec Sheet button stays bottom-left — asked and declined 2026-10-25

Shak asked to move it to the top right on phone "like desktop". **Declined after measuring, because the
desktop arrangement cannot be reproduced on a phone.**

**IT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A STYLE TOGGLE.** `Profile Row` (`/fixtures`) and `Elements Row` (`/elements`) each
hold three children — `Media`, `Info`, `Downloads`:

| | stackDirection | Media | Info | Downloads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop | horizontal | `2fr` | `1fr` | `212px` @ top 16 |
| Tablet | horizontal | `2fr` | `1fr` | `180px` @ top 16 |
| **Phone** | **vertical** | `1fr` | `1fr` | `1fr` @ **top 481** |

Desktop puts the button level with the title because all three start at `top: 16` in a horizontal row. Phone
flips the row to vertical, so `Downloads` falls to the bottom. That is the whole mechanism.

**!!! THE BLOCKER IS THE TITLE WIDTH, AND IT IS THE PART THAT IS NOT OBVIOUS. !!!** At 390px the title column
is 350 and the longest names already fill it — `Vena Corner Mini` **339px of ink**, `Prisma Multiplier` 330,
`Vena Round Mini` 329. A 111px button beside the title would sit on the text. **So "level with the title" is
unreachable at any phone width**; desktop only works because the title gets its own 397px column and the
button a third column beside it. Measure the title's INK, not its box — the box is full-width on every one.

"Top right" on phone therefore means the top-right of the **row**, which is over the technical-drawing card.
Simulated in the live DOM before offering: it lands on the card's empty corner and covers no artwork, only the
border. Offered with a side-by-side render against two alternatives and declined — the button stays where it is.

**SIX INDEPENDENT ROW TEMPLATES, NOT ONE SHARED COMPONENT.** All plain `FrameNode`s with
`componentIdentifier: null` — `/fixtures` Flex `s4lEM1w_G` / Profile `kiCM4bfas` / Optic `U9_Nm6dyA`,
`/elements` Connector `rZiLJanmS` / Driver `NmkizI7ok` / LED `E8VN4fVoI`. Any change here is **six edits**.
Per-breakpoint overrides do work (phone already carries its own `stackDirection: vertical`), but **moving
`Downloads` is NOT per-breakpoint** — a node has one parent, and moving it into `Info` would take `Media`
from 795 to 963 on desktop and enlarge every product image.

**If it is ever revisited, anchor from the BOTTOM, not the top.** All 16 products are geometrically uniform on
phone (`Info` 264 tall, title 48 = one line, `Media` 169), and `rowH - titleTop` is a constant **280** because
`Media`'s height cancels out of it — whereas a `top` anchor drifts about 20px across 360-430px phones, since
`Media` is aspect-driven at `(rowWidth - 12) / 2`.

### THE NAV NEVER WENT BACK TO TRANSPARENT ON 25 OF 27 SURFACES — Framer omits a variant's `backgroundColor` when it is inherited rather than explicit (2026-10-22, PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED LIVE)

Shak: *"when scrolling back to the top the nav bar does not transition back to original state in certain instances"*, with a
screenshot of a white bar over the dark Home hero.

**IT WAS 25 OF 27 LIVE SURFACES — every desktop, every tablet, and 7 of 9 phones.** The two that worked are `/` phone and
`/contact` phone. Scrolling back to the top left the bar **solid white** (black on `/contact`) permanently — still stuck at
20 seconds, so genuinely stranded rather than a slow fade.

**!!! MY PASS CRITERION COMPARED THE VARIANT NAME, SO THE FIRST 27-SURFACE SWEEP REPORTED "ok" ON EVERYTHING. !!!**

The `data-framer-name` reverts correctly on **all 27** — `Fill White` back to `Nav black`, class `framer-v-13gtcbd` back to
`framer-v-1uu4b65`. Only the **paint** strands. So every sweep I have run on this since 2026-10-18 was measuring the half
of the state that was never broken.

**The rule: verify a Framer variant revert by the COMPUTED/INLINE STYLE, never by the variant name or class.** A name is a
label on the state machine; the animation is what carries the style, and the two can disagree in exactly this way. Same
family as the already-recorded "`data-framer-name` is the instance WRAPPER and never changes" trap, one level deeper.

**THE ROOT CAUSE IS IN THE COMPILED CHUNK, AND NOTHING ON THE CANVAS SHOWS IT.** The nav root compiles to a base `style`
plus a `variants` map, and **a variant only gets an entry for a property it sets EXPLICITLY**. Pre-fix:

```js
style:{backdropFilter:`none`,backgroundColor:`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`,WebkitBackdropFilter:`none`,...},
variants:{
  CKhcbJTh3:{backdropFilter:`none`,WebkitBackdropFilter:`none`},          <- no backgroundColor
  dAgREWuQT:{backdropFilter:`none`,WebkitBackdropFilter:`none`},          <- no backgroundColor
  Fi3YBzeYn:{backdropFilter:`blur(40px)`,backgroundColor:`rgb(0, 0, 0)`,...},      <- Fill Black
  lQ7T5v16X:{backdropFilter:`blur(40px)`,backgroundColor:`rgb(255, 255, 255)`,...} <- Fill White
  ...}
```

**Only the two `Fill` variants declare `backgroundColor`.** Motion animating *to* a variant that omits a property has no
target for it, so it leaves it where it is — at the solid colour the fill just set. `backdrop-filter` reverts correctly
because **every** variant declares it, which is why the bar visibly loses its blur while keeping its colour and reads as a
half-finished animation.

**WHY THE TWO WORKING SURFACES WORK, and it is the clue that cracks it:** `/` phone and `/contact` phone are the only two
resting on **`CQn2PSQz8` (`Nav white`), which is the DEFAULT variant**. A default has no entry in the map at all — its
values *are* the base `style`, and the base **does** carry `backgroundColor: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`. So those two revert
through the base and the other 25 revert through an entry with the property missing.

**THE CANVAS AND THE API BOTH REPORTED THE EIGHT AS TRANSPARENT.** `setAttributes` read `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` on every one —
the inherited base value — while the compiled chunk emitted nothing. **So "the stored value is correct" is not evidence
the property will animate**; what matters is whether the variant sets it *explicitly*. The API cannot distinguish
inherited from explicit, so the compiled chunk is the only oracle.

**THE FIX: write a DISTINCT-BUT-EQUIVALENT literal to force materialisation.** Eight variants (`glROJL_vL` Hide,
`OTFjEScTr` Nav Load, `TVfWqaIfB` Hide black, `dAgREWuQT` Nav load black, `CKhcbJTh3` Nav black, `RmynPz7kD` Hide white,
`nTYo4Lp5J` Nav load white, `gDOEOKgPj` Nav white) set to **`rgba(255, 255, 255, 0)`** — visually identical to
`rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`, textually different. Post-fix all eight emit `backgroundColor: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0)`.

**`CQn2PSQz8` was deliberately NOT touched** — it is the default, so its value is the base style, it already works, and
writing it would change the base for every variant that inherits it.

**Whether writing the identical `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` would also have materialised it is UNTESTED.** A different literal
guaranteed it; equality with the base is the condition I was trying to break, so matching it was the one thing not worth
risking.

**I HAD A CONFIDENT WRONG HYPOTHESIS AND THE CHUNK IS WHAT KILLED IT.** 300ms sampling showed every broken surface passing
through `Nav Load` / `Nav load black` on the way back, and the instance variant correlated with broken/working **27 of 27**
— so I concluded the appear chain (`Hide -> Nav Load -> Nav white`) was re-firing and interrupting the revert. The
correlation was real and the causation was backwards: those two instance variants correlate because they are the only ones
resting on the default. **Had I acted on it I would have dropped the hairline draw-in AND it would still have been broken
on every black-ink page, since `CQn2PSQz8` is the white-ink variant.** A 27-of-27 correlation on a 2-vs-25 split is one bit
of information; it felt like proof.

**The appear chain was never touched and is intact** — `glROJL_vL` is still registered, and the hairline's
`.framer-v-fo6u7a .framer-18ryws4 { width: 0% }` rule still ships.

**HONEST CAVEAT I CANNOT CLOSE: I do not know whether this regressed or had been broken all along.** My 2026-10-18 and
2026-10-20 verifications both record the back-state as "transparent" — but both recorded it **by variant name**, which was
correct on every surface the whole time. There is no measurement in this file of the back-state's actual colour before
today, so neither reading can be supported.

**Verified:** 27-surface sweep comparing background colour, **0 failures of 27**; Home captured with all videos frozen at
`currentTime = 1.0` showing transparent -> solid white -> transparent (rest 71,497 B / scrolled 6,233 B / back 71,438 B);
full Home regression sweep 15/15. Published as `fab035092`, preview guarded to exactly one change naming
`Navigation / Navigation Desktop`.

**Noted, not acted on: `/news/:slug` phone still renders `Navigation Mobile` / `Navigation White`** — a solid white bar,
inconsistent with the phone-nav standardisation that moved every other page onto the desktop component. The CMS template
pages were not in that pass.

the folder.

**!!! NEITHER PROFILE THICKNESS, END-CAP SPAN NOR AUTOCORRELATION PITCH CAN SIZE A REPEATING CHAIN
WHOSE PROJECTION HAS CHANGED. !!!**

The six non-chain drawings sized first time — `geo` for the four contained ones, profile thickness
for Flow Spine and Flow Straight, all confirmed by eye. The two Prisma Links took four attempts:

| metric | PL1 frame | rendered |
|---|---|---|
| profile thickness (median per-column vertical span) | 653 | **too big** |

| autocorrelation pitch | 1141 | **too small** — locked onto a 3:2 harmonic |
| **chosen by eye from a scale ladder** | **600** | correct |

Each metric is 1-D and each is contaminated differently once the viewing angle changes: profile by
module overlap, end-cap span by the foreshortening of the end face, pitch by the chain's own
periodicity. **The new chains are drawn flatter and longer than the ones they replace, so MODULE
SIZE and MODULE COUNT cannot both be matched** — at F=700 PL1 shows the live drawing's six modules
at 85% of their size; at F=600 it shows five at full size. **Module size won, because that is the
product; the count is an artifact of how much run the vendor happened to draw.**

**THE SCALE LADDER IS THE INSTRUMENT, AND IT SHOULD BE REACHED FOR SOONER.** Rendering one row of
candidate frames beside the live asset **at the true 587 device-px card** answered in one screenshot
what three metrics and five exec round trips could not. **Judge it at 587** — a first ladder drawn
at 293px was actively misleading and reversed the apparent direction of the error.

**Stroke: the established vector convention, unchanged** — `1.00` device px at `#999999`, giving
darkest `154-156` on the hosted assets against `154-158` for the six cross-sections already live.
Confirmed by eye against four of them before publishing; the whole 14-drawing vector set now reads
as one family.

**`perStroke` IS WORTHLESS ON NEAR-HORIZONTAL LINE ART AND SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN REPORTED AS A
CONTROL.** Flow Straight measures `1.329` against `0.388` for Driver 5-1 at the identical stroke
setting, because a horizontal scan line runs **along** a shallow diagonal and returns its length.
This is the documented trap, and the drawings that trip it are exactly the long extrusions.
**Use darkest-pixel and the eye for a vector drawing's weight; per-stroke ink only compares
drawings of similar line direction.**

**Delivered and verified.** Hosted: every frame byte-identical in size to the asset it replaced
(`2000/1805/1723/1745/1890/1783/1360/900`), `minAlpha 255` and four white corners on all eight so
the lightbox requirement holds, geometry matching the built values exactly. Draft counts clean on
all eight collections. Publish preview guarded to exactly eight `CollectionItem` changes — it
returned exactly those and nothing from the other session.

**THE BYTE DELTA RECONCILED TO ZERO, AND THIS TIME THE BASELINE EXISTED.** `/products` `-124`,
`/elements` `-60`. With the publish comment normalised and the eight asset ids mapped old->new,
**both pages are exactly the same length** with **8 differing runs each, every one build metadata**:

x3. **Zero content change.** Home byte-identical at `275,308`, sweep 14/14.

**A naive id-length sum did NOT account for the delta (`-12` of `-124`) and that is not a
discrepancy — an asset id appears more often than its srcset references**, since the serialised CMS
payload carries it too. **Normalise and diff; do not try to predict a delta from a reference count.**

**THREE SELF-INFLICTED FAILURES, ALL ALREADY WRITTEN IN THIS FILE:**

### RENDER CURRENCY AUDIT — the two Prisma Links are five weeks older than anything else, and a `.png` extension is what hid them (2026-10-22)

Shak: *"do you have prisma link 1 and 2 (viper 1 and viper 2) updated renders?"* **No, and the
answer corrects a gap list I had given him an hour earlier.**

**THE FULL PROVENANCE OF ALL 16 PRODUCT PHOTOS, traced to the Drive source rather than read off
the CMS:**

| | render source | dated |
|---|---|---|
| 9 fixtures (Vena x5, Flow x3, Prisma Multiplier) | `Product Renders\Web Ready` E-13…E-22 | **14-19 Oct** |
| Rima 5 + Rima 10 | E-16 | 18 Oct |
| Liga T, Liga W, Driver 5-1 | the `JPG\Revision Round B-*` batch | 8 Oct |
| **Prisma Link 1 + 2** | **`Product Lines\Darkened 75\Viper`** | **12 SEPTEMBER** |

**So five products need renders, not three.** I had reported `liga-t, liga-w, driver-5-1` and
missed the two oldest assets on the site. The sweep that settles it is one `find` over the whole
`Products` tree printing mtimes — the newest image anywhere is E-22 on 19 Oct, and `Web Ready`
holds exactly ten files, none of them a Viper.

**!!! THE EXTENSION LIED, AND IT LIED BECAUSE OF MY OWN WORK. !!!**

The E-batch landed as `.png` while the stale October Elements photos stayed `.jpg`, so `.jpg`
became a usable shorthand for "not refreshed" — and on 2026-10-21 I used exactly that shorthand,
recording *"nine on the new `.png` assets with the two Prisma Links untouched on `.jpg`"*. By the
end of that same day the end-cap alignment pass had **rebuilt all eleven, the Prisma Links
included**, emitting PNG. They then read as current in every later check.

**A derived asset's format and date record the last PROCESSING pass, not the provenance of its
content.** The Prisma Link photos are September pixels in an October container. **To date a render
you must trace it back to the source file in Drive; the CMS binding cannot tell you.**

**The second reason it hid: these two renders have never been in `Product Renders` at all.** They
are filed under `Product Lines\Darkened 75\Viper`, beside the drawings, because that folder was
delivered as a drawing batch that happened to contain two `- Rendered -` files. **A per-folder
sweep of the renders directory is structurally incapable of finding them** — the same shape as the
`/products` + `/elements` nav defect, where a consistency check could not see a fault that was
consistent. **Sweep by product, never by folder.**

**THE RESOLUTION GAP IS THE REAL COST AND IT IS LARGE:**

```
Viper renders    2000 x 2000       <- Prisma Link 1 + 2
E-batch renders  8000 x 8000       <- 16x the pixels
```

After the end-cap crop the two Viper windows are only ~1024 and ~900 source px against a 587
device-px card, putting them at the bottom of the set's `1.63-2.92x` oversampling range. Adequate
today, no headroom, and the only two products on the site in that position. **The replacement ask
specifies 8000x8000 so they match the rest.**

**Note this is a DIFFERENT axis from the drawing-currency note above it.** That one ends *"still
without replacement artwork: Rima 5 and Rima 10… everything else is now vector-sourced"*, which is
true of **drawings**. The two statements are complementary and neither is the whole picture:

```

fully current    the other nine fixtures
```

### THE `/contact` FORM WAS DEAD — remote pre-audit module AND an empty form id, both fixed (2026-10-22, PUBLISHED `b009e3772`)

Shak pointed at the teaser's working form and asked for it to be pulled across. **Two separate faults, and fixing
only the obvious one would have been worse than leaving it alone.**

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| component | `module:UflTnc38Mi5sDIwszK8J/…/FormSpark.js:default` — **REMOTE, pre-audit** | **`local-module:codeFile/TnK637F:default`** |
| `formId` | **`""`** — the form POSTed nowhere | **`75jmfofPI`** |
| failed submission | would have reported **success** | shows an error, keeps the form |

**THE SEQUENCING MATTERED, AND IT IS THE REASON NOT TO JUST PASTE THE ID IN.** The repo's `FormSpark.tsx`
carries the `response.ok` check added after the June–October 2026 incident; the remote copy does not. Setting
`formId` alone would have produced a form that sends correctly on the happy path and **still tells a visitor
their enquiry was sent when it failed** — the exact defect that was live on www.alkimiworks.com for four months.
**A dead form is more honest than a lying one, so the component swap had to come first.** Proven from the
published chunk before touching anything: `Something went wrong` **0**, `role="alert"` **0**, `.ok` **0**.

**`componentIdentifier` IS NOT WRITABLE — second independent confirmation.** `setAttributes` returned
`writeError=none` and a separate-`exec` read-back showed all three still remote. Editor-only.

**!!! A SINGLE LOGICAL INSTANCE GETS NO CONFIRMATION DIALOG — the swap applied the moment the component was
clicked. !!!** Every previous replace-all in this project put up a count ("19 instances", "all 2 instances") and
the standing rule is to cancel one whose count you cannot account for. **Here there was nothing to cancel.** So
the dialog is not a guaranteed checkpoint: **establish the instance count BEFORE opening the menu**, not from the
dialog. Here it was known to be 1 logical instance (`POi5p3t1V` plus two breakpoint copies) from the pre-state.

**THIS SWAP PRESERVED EVERYTHING — a third data point, and the variance still has no pattern.** All **15**
control keys survived with byte-identical values on all three breakpoints, diffed against
[repair/formspark-prestate-2026-10-22.json](repair/formspark-prestate-2026-10-22.json). The footer swap reset
`variant` on all 6; the Primary Button swap preserved everything; this preserved everything. **Capture the
pre-state and diff, every time** — and note the swap assigns **new node ids** (`POi5p3t1V -> WOyYtl0HY`), so the
diff must key on (page, path, component), never on id.

**THE RECORDED WARNING ABOUT GREPPING THE SERVED HTML FOR THE FORM ID IS CONFIRMED, AND NOW EXPLAINED.** After
publishing, `grep 75jmfofPI contact.html` returns **0** on a page whose form demonstrably works. It is a property
control, so Framer compiles it into the **page's JS chunk** as a prop in the component's props object —
`…,formId:\`75jmfofPI\`,gap:12,height:\`100%\`,id:\`WOyYtl0HY\`,…` — never into the markup. **Scan the chunks, not
the page.** The chunk is found by sweeping every `.mjs` the page references for a distinctive literal.

**The decisive proof is the minified ternary**, which distinguishes the fixed component from the pre-audit one
in a single expression:

```js
fetch(`https://api.formspark.io/${n}`,{method:`POST`,…})
  .then(e=>{ e.ok ? (F(!0), y?.()) : (P(!1), R(!0)) })
  .catch(()=>{ P(!1), R(!0) })
```

`e.ok ?` is the check; `y?.()` is the guarded `onSubmit?.()`; the `.catch` covers a network failure. The
pre-audit version was `.then(() => { setSuccess(true); onSubmit() })` with no check and no catch.

**!!! THE RECORDED TEST RECIPE CREATES A REAL ENQUIRY ON THE SUCCESS PATH — USE REQUEST INTERCEPTION FOR BOTH
PATHS INSTEAD. !!!** This file's `fetch` monkeypatch forces a 500 for the failure path and then says to use a
**real 200** for the success path, which sends a genuine enquiry to Formspark every time anyone re-tests.
Playwright's `page.route` fakes both, so neither path reaches Formspark and the request itself is inspectable:

```js
await p.route('**api.formspark.io**', async (route) => {
  hit = { url: route.request().url(), method: route.request().method(), body: route.request().postData() };
  await route.fulfill({ status, contentType: 'application/json', body: '{}' });
});
```

**Capturing the intercepted request is the part that proves the form id is wired** — stronger than any grep,
because it is the URL the browser actually built:

| | failure path (forced 500) | success path (faked 200) |
|---|---|---|
| request | `POST api.formspark.io/75jmfofPI` with the real JSON body | identical |
| form | **stays**, 1 name input | **removed**, 0 inputs |
| message field | **preserved** | — |
| `role="alert"` | **1** — *"Something went wrong — please try again."* | **0** |
| success tick | — | present |

returned `CDP sendCommand "Runtime.evaluate" timed out after 45000ms`. This file's advice is to stop driving the
editor; **better is to leave the frozen tab alone and open your own** — a fresh tab deep-linked to the same page
mounted cleanly (`innerWidth 1536`, 3,240 divs) and drove without trouble. Only abandon the job if a *fresh* tab
is also unusable. `Page.captureScreenshot` still froze once mid-task, and reading the menu from the DOM carried

**A layer-tree walk is the reliable way to reach this layer**, since the search box does not hold its filter on a
plain page: `Desktop -> Main -> Section CTA -> Content Wrapper -> Stack[1] -> FormSpark`, expanding by the
disclosure arrow at `row.x - 16` with ~800 ms between steps. **Both `Stack` children share a name**, so the
second was selected by position, not by text.

### `/news/:slug` BROUGHT ONTO THE STANDARD NAV — the last surface, and it was a bigger gap than "two attributes" (2026-10-22, PUBLISHED `eebdd110c`)

The article template was the only live page still rendering `Navigation Mobile` on phone. Measuring before
touching anything showed the gap was wider than the open-items note claimed:

```
DESKTOP   transparent -> Fill White -> back     but fired at 300px, on #trigger
TABLET    same                                   fired at 300px
PHONE     solid white bar, never transitioned
```

Its ids were `hero, trigger, overlay` with **no `*-nav-state`** — so this page was never in the 40px
standardisation pass at all. Nine live pages had a `Navigation Scroll Trigger`; this was the only one without.

**THE INK QUESTION LOOKED HARD AND WAS SETTLED BY ONE MEASUREMENT.** A CMS template must serve every article,
and the three live ones have different heroes (two video, one image), all dark imagery — so "what colour is
the nav over" reads as unanswerable in general. It is not: **`Section Hero` carries `padding: 150px 45px 0 45px`**,
so the band behind the nav is the template's own white padding, not the article's artwork. Simulated by hiding
the nav in the DOM and sampling the strip: **mean/min/max luminance `255` on all three articles.** Black ink,
unambiguous, for any article now or later.

**Final state — identical to `/news`, its own listing page:** `Hide black` at rest (transparent, black ink),
`Section in view / Viewport top / Replay Yes` on `#article-nav-state`, `To: Fill White`, fires at **39px** on
all three breakpoints and reverts.

**!!! THE SCROLL SECTION NAME IS NOT EXPOSED THROUGH THE NODE API. !!!** A full key dump of the trigger node
returns the usual 60-odd layout keys and nothing resembling it, and a string scan for `nav-state` across every
attribute returns nothing on all three breakpoints. Add it to the blind list beside appear effects, variant
transitions, CMS bindings, conditional visibility, canvas text, vectors, page SEO fields and `pointer`.
**The option list in another effect's `Section` dropdown is the cheapest oracle** — it lists every section on
the page by name, and the option's `value` is the trigger node's own id.

**!!! THE VIEWPORT CONTROL: SET IT EXPLICITLY, NEVER INFER IT. !!!** Its three buttons carry
**`aria-label="Top" / "Center" / "Bottom"`** — so the *identity* of each button is readable, while the recorded
"no DOM signal" remains true of the *state* (all three report `bg rgba(0,0,0,0)`, `opacity 1`, `svg fill none`,
before and after a click). That asymmetry is the useful part: **a click on `Top` is idempotent, so setting it
costs nothing and removes the need to read it.** The alternative — solving Viewport from the old 300px fire
point — is arithmetic on a value you cannot check, and getting it wrong is the `/about` filled-at-rest defect.
The 39px threshold measured after publishing is what confirms `Top` took.

**THE `Section` REFERENCE DID CASCADE THIS TIME, which narrows a rule recorded as four-for-four.** Tablet and
Phone both already read `#article-nav-state` after only Desktop was set. The reconciliation: a breakpoint that
holds **its own stored Section** blocks the cascade and must be set explicitly; one that merely inherits picks
it up. So the standing advice — always read all three — is right, but "it never cascades" was the wrong reason.

**A PLAIN `visible: false` LAYER STILL RENDERS ITS PROPERTY CONTROLS.** The recorded blank-panel case
(*"a component instance's property controls are not rendered at all while the layer is hidden"*) was a
**condition**-hidden layer. Phone's hidden desktop-nav showed its full `Effects` section, so the effect could
be configured *before* the visibility flip — which is what kept every intermediate state publishable-safe:
trigger pasted (invisible) -> effects wired (targeting a hidden instance, a no-op) -> flip last.

**!!! A CODE-FILE EDIT RETURNS `changesCount: 0` FROM THE PUBLISH PREVIEW AND STILL SHIPS. !!!**

Four consecutive reads on a **fresh** session returned `count 0, changes []` with an identical confirmation hash —

This is a new row, and it **narrows the 2026-10-19 `/404` rule rather than extending it**:

| change | preview / counter sees it | publishes |
|---|---|---|
| page-level layer property (padding, visible, draft) | yes | yes |
| component-internal layer property | no | **yes** |
| page-level instance control (a label, an href) | yes | yes |
| **code file via `setFileContent`** | **no** | **YES** |
| page-level instance **`variant`** control | no | **NO — needs an editor round trip** |

**So invisibility does not predict publishability, and `variant` remains the sole known exception.** The byte
count after publishing is the only authority either way.

**IT ALSO MEANS THE PREVIEW CANNOT SERVE AS THE COLLISION DETECTOR FOR A CODE CHANGE**, since there is nothing of
yours for it to show. The substitute used here: **diff all 8 code files against the repo by LF-normalised byte
count** — 8/8 matched, proving the other session had not touched the code layer. The publish was then guarded to
abort if the preview showed **anything at all**, on the reasoning that any visible change could not be mine.

| form | **stays**, 4 inputs, message preserved | **removed** |
| `role="alert"` | **1** — *"Something went wrong — please try again."* | **0** |

The `response.ok` guard from the form-wiring work is intact and the notice interferes with neither path.

Nothing clips it (`clipAncestor: null`, `form` overflow `visible`), and it is one line everywhere. **But there is

Verified: notice on `/contact` only (0 on all seven other live pages), `/privacy` returns 200, Home byte-identical

**THE GENERATED-ESCAPE TRAP FIRED TWICE MORE, AND THE SECOND TIME WAS A PATCHER PATCHING A PATCHER.** A `\r\n`
written into a generated script came back as a real CRLF inside a string literal (`SyntaxError: Invalid or
unexpected token`). The recorded fix is the one that worked: **delete the generator and rewrite it from a quoted
heredoc with no escape sequences at all** — `String.fromCharCode(13)`, `String.fromCharCode(10)`, and template
literals carrying real newlines for every anchor. **Do not patch the patcher.** The guard then did its job
honestly: the first run aborted with `ABORT: anchor props matched 0 times` because the repo is CRLF and the
anchors were LF — a refusal, not a silent mis-write.

**Embedding a 26KB file in an `exec` script is safe via `JSON.stringify`**, because node does the escaping rather
than you: generate `const CODE = ` + `JSON.stringify(source)` straight to a file with `fs.writeFileSync`, with no
heredoc layer over the content.

**CORRECTION — `browser_run_code_unsafe` TAKES `code`, AND `TypeError: __fn__ is not a function` MEANS THE
PARAMETER WAS MISSING OR MISNAMED.** This file records that tool as having "failed all session" on 2026-10-20 with
exactly that error, and treats it as situational flakiness. **It is almost certainly the same mistake**: the
server evaluates `undefined` as a function when `code` is absent. The tool works, takes
`async (page) => { ... }`, and reaches `page.context().browser().newContext()` — so the
fresh-context-per-breakpoint rule **is** available through it.

**!!! THE REUSABLE TECHNIQUE: INTERCEPT THE FILE-INPUT CLICK. !!!** Clicking an `Upload` button opens a
native OS file dialog that automation cannot see, dismiss, or recover from — it can wedge the browser.
Patch the prototype first and the dialog never opens, while the click still tells you which input Framer
armed:

```js
window.__origClick = HTMLInputElement.prototype.click;
HTMLInputElement.prototype.click = function () {
  if (this.type === 'file') { window.__cap = { fired: true, el: this }; return; }   // swallowed
  return window.__origClick.apply(this, arguments);
};
```

**Framer has exactly ONE `input[type=file]` in the whole document and repurposes it per slot** — before the
click it has no `accept`; after clicking a slot's `Upload` it carries the image MIME list. So the order is
forced: **click the slot's Upload button (armed), then feed the input.** Feeding it without clicking first
would land in no slot or the wrong one.

**Feed it with the `file_upload` tool and a `ref`, never by embedding base64.** The client reads the local
file itself, so nothing enters context. `find` locates the hidden input fine despite it being `0x0`.

**!!! THE CDN NEVER RETURNS AN ASSET'S ORIGINAL BYTES — so you cannot round-trip to get byte-identity.
!!!** Three fetch variants of a 33,906-byte master all returned **10,038 bytes**:

```
plain, ?lossless=1, and Accept: image/png   ->  10,038 B every time
```

That is why the local file had to be the source: feeding a derivative back would have **permanently stored
a degraded favicon**, since whatever you upload becomes the master.

**A CONTEXT MENU'S FIRST ITEM IS NOT PRE-HIGHLIGHTED — one `Down` lands on item 1.** This file records the
opposite for *submenus* ("the first item is already highlighted, so `Down` selects the second"), and that
nearly caused a wrong pick here. **The two behave differently; check which you are in by zooming before
pressing `Return`.** Confirmed again that a real `computer left_click` **dismisses a Framer popover without

### THE FAVICON AND CARD — built pad-only, and the variant choice was settled by a failure test

**Source: the A glyph from the wordmark, never the `_icon_` files.** All four `Alkimi_icon_*` assets in
Drive are **bleed crops** (`L0.0 R3.8 T0.5 B0.0`), so the crossbar runs off the left and the A's right leg
off the bottom — at 32px that reads as a rendering error. In `logo_big.png` (byte-identical to
`Alkimi wordmark - black.png`, same md5) the glyph sits cleanly at **`x 0..1758, y 2..1315`** with a clear
gap before the `L`, confirmed identical in the white sibling.

So the favicon is a **pure crop + pad at 1900x1900 with no scaling anywhere** — the mark reaches Framer at
native resolution having never touched a resampler. **Shak asked for the crossbar flush to the left
boundary**: ink starts at `x = 0` exactly, right margin 7.42%, vertically centred. That also made the mark
~10% larger in frame than a centred version, and the bar running off the edge matches how the wordmark
itself is drawn.

**Use the native white wordmark for light-on-dark, never a `lutrgb` flip of the black one** — it is the
designer's own asset with its own antialiasing. Verify the two files' glyph runs match before cropping
either; here they were identical.

**!!! THE VARIANT CHOICE WAS DECIDED BY TESTING THE FAILURE MODE, NOT BY TASTE. !!!** Rendered at 16px on
mismatched chrome, **both transparent variants are effectively invisible** — black-A on dark chrome, white-A
on light chrome. That is not hypothetical: Framer emits the two icons distinguished **only by a `media`
attribute**, and iOS Safari, bookmark managers, feed readers and link scrapers often ignore it, so half the
audience would see nothing. **The solid `#080200` tile renders identically on both chromes and has no
mismatch case to fail**, holds at 16px because the tile carries when the hairline softens, and collapses the
light/dark pair into one file. It is also the right answer for the apple touch icon, since iOS composites
transparency onto white.

**The card is 1200x630 at 50% wordmark width, and the square crop decided that.** Several clients centre-crop
a 1.91:1 card to a square thumbnail; at 62% that **severs the crossbar and the `©`**, at 50% the whole
lockup survives (`x 300..899` inside the crop window `285..914`) and still holds the full card. Fill verified
exactly `8,2,0` on all four corners and all four mid-edges — the `lavfi color` source was force-corrected
with `lutrgb=r=8:g=2:b=0`, so none of the documented YUV drift got in. **Stayed at 1200x630 rather than 2x
deliberately**: Slack, LinkedIn and Twitter render unfurls at ~360-520 CSS px, so even doubled for retina a
1200px card is already oversampled.

Both were verified on the **hosted** copies by `createImageBitmap` in a browser, with no ffmpeg in the path.

### THE SITE TITLE AND DESCRIPTION ARE SET — Shak's copy, live on all 12 surfaces (2026-10-22)

**This CLOSES the "every description is empty" item recorded in the section above, which is now stale.**

Verified by re-deriving from the live site, not from the editor: **all 12 pages carry the description on

from the News template's own SEO Title, which is a literal and not derived from the site title.

**!!! THE DESCRIPTION META TAGS WERE THERE ALL ALONG, AS BARE `content` ATTRIBUTES — which is why the
earlier "empty" reading was ambiguous and why my byte prediction was 114 out. !!!**

```
BEFORE   <meta name="description" content>                 33 chars
AFTER    <meta name="description" content="Measured …">   104 chars
```

An attribute-reading helper that looks for `content="` finds nothing in `content>` and returns `null`;
a helper that returns `""` for "no tag found" reports the identical thing. **So `""` from a meta reader
means EITHER an absent tag OR a valueless one, and the two cannot be told apart without printing the raw
tag.** Print the tag, not the parsed value, whenever absence is the thing being established.

**THE DELTA RECONCILES TO THE CHARACTER against the saved pre-publish copy** — `275,288 -> 275,642`
UTF-16 length, **+354**, covering both of today's metadata publishes:

```
3 description tags   33->104, 40->111, 41->112      +213
og:title + twitter:title   43->54, 44->55            +22
<title>                                              +11
apple-touch-icon <link>  (earlier publish)           +89
two publishes of build churn                         +19
                                                    ----
                                                     354
```

**A `<link>` IS NOT A `<meta>`, so a meta-tag diff is silently blind to the apple-touch-icon.** The two
asset-id swaps and the two searchIndex renames contributed **zero** — same-length strings on both sides.

`275,642` JS characters; the file holds 20 multibyte characters. The figures recorded in this file come
from `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf8").length`, so **comparing `stat().size` against a recorded figure is off
by the multibyte count** — here it manufactured a 20-byte discrepancy on top of the real one. Measure both
sides the same way.

**WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS: the description is IDENTICAL on all 12 pages.** Correct
for a site-level default, and weakest on the three articles, where a search result now shows company
